subject: The land register beats the fence: a boundary is where the register and the survey put it, not where a fence has stood
bears_on: case_orchard page 2 (the 2019 survey placing the fence 3.2 m west of the registered line; the claimant does not contest the measurement but argues long use) and page 3 (the fence in place since 1991)
titelzeile: Boundary dispute: the registered boundary prevails over a fence standing off the line for decades
leitsatz: The boundary of a parcel runs where the land register and the cadastral survey place it. A fence that has stood off the registered line for decades neither moves the boundary nor founds a presumption that the line runs along it; the presumption of § 891 BGB attaches to the register, not to the fence.

Long and undisturbed use of a strip beyond the registered boundary is possession, not title. It gives the user no right to possession under § 986 BGB, no defence against the registered owner's claims under § 985 and § 1004 BGB, and no ownership that a declaration under § 256 ZPO could confirm.
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau, 2. Zivilkammer, of 14 May 2008 – 2 O 155/07 – is dismissed.
The plaintiff shall bear the costs of the appeal proceedings. The apportionment of the costs of the first instance in the judgment under appeal remains unaffected.

This judgment and the judgment under appeal are provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum enforceable, unless the defendant first provides security in the same amount.
The revision is not admitted. The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set at 9,000 euros.

tatbestand.text: The parties are neighbouring farmers in the district of Grevenau and dispute the ownership of a strip of land along their common boundary. The plaintiff, the market gardener K., is the registered owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry; the defendant, the farm of the family Mertens, is the registered owner of the adjoining parcel 87/2 to the east. Between the parcels runs a wire fence on concrete posts of about 140 metres in length which, as is undisputed, has stood in its present line since at least 1974. West of the fence the plaintiff and, before him, his father have cultivated the land, laid a drainage channel and made a farm track along the fence.

In autumn 2006 the defendant had the boundary between the parcels located by a public surveyor. The surveyor's plan of 9 November 2006 places the fence, along its whole length, between 2.8 and 3.1 metres east of the registered boundary; the strip between fence and registered line, of about 400 square metres, is therefore by the geometry of the register part of parcel 87/2. The plaintiff does not contest the measurement. He contends that the fence has marked the boundary for as long as anyone remembers, that the register must for that reason be wrong, and that the strip has in any event been in the exclusive and undisturbed use of his family for more than thirty years without objection from the defendant or its predecessors.

The plaintiff sought a declaration that the strip belongs to parcel 87/1 and, in the alternative, an order that the defendant consent to the correction of the land register. The defendant, by counterclaim, sought the surrender of the strip and an order that the plaintiff refrain from cultivating it and from driving on it. The chamber, by the judgment under appeal, dismissed the action and allowed the counterclaim. It held that the presumption of § 891 BGB operated in favour of the defendant and had not been rebutted, since neither the position of the fence nor the plaintiff's use of the strip proved that the register was wrong. With his appeal the plaintiff pursues his claims in full and seeks the dismissal of the counterclaim. The defendant defends the judgment.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in due form and time (§§ 511, 517, 519, 520 ZPO). It is, however, unfounded. The chamber was right to treat the declaratory action as admissible. The plaintiff has the interest required by § 256 Abs. 1 ZPO, because the defendant disputes his ownership of the strip by having the boundary surveyed and by pursuing its counterclaim, so that a declaration would settle the parties' legal relationship with regard to the strip. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to that declaration is a question of the merits, and on the merits the chamber decided correctly.
II. 1.

The boundary of a parcel is the registered boundary. The land register identifies each parcel by reference to the official cadastre (§ 2 Abs. 2 GBO), and the cadastral survey carries that line onto the ground. Two questions must be kept apart. That the defendant is the owner of parcel 87/2 is presumed under § 891 Abs. 1 BGB from the entry in the register; where the boundary of that parcel runs is proved by the publicly appointed surveyor's plan of the cadastral geometry, which the plaintiff does not contest and which the Senate is free to evaluate under § 286 ZPO. The plan places the fence about three metres east of the registered line. The strip therefore lies within parcel 87/2, and it was for the plaintiff to rebut the presumption in the defendant's favour.

The plaintiff has not rebutted the presumption. Rebuttal requires proof that the register is wrong: that the entry rests on a failed transfer, that the parcels were divided otherwise than the cadastre records, that the boundary was carried into the survey wrongly, or that it was legally fixed in another line. A fence proves none of this. It is a fact of use, not an act of disposition; nobody acquires land by fencing it. Nor does a fence found a presumption that the boundary runs along it: §§ 921, 922 BGB presuppose a boundary and govern what stands on it, and § 920 BGB applies only where the true boundary cannot be ascertained, whereas here the survey has ascertained it. What stood off the line in 1974 stands off the line today.

The plaintiff's use of the strip for more than thirty years is possession, not title. Land is acquired by lapse of time only under § 900 Abs. 1 BGB, which requires thirty years of registration as owner together with proprietary possession; the plaintiff has never been registered as owner of the strip. Mere use, however long and undisturbed, transfers nothing. It gives the plaintiff no right to possession under § 986 BGB and no defence to the defendant's claims for surrender under § 985 BGB and for cessation of the cultivation and crossing under § 1004 Abs. 1 BGB. The tolerance of the defendant's predecessors was at most a revocable licence. The claims of a registered owner are not subject to limitation (§ 902 Abs. 1 BGB), and lapse of time alone does not found forfeiture under § 242 BGB.
III.

The alternative claim fails for the same reason. § 894 BGB gives a claim to consent to the correction of the register only where its content departs from the true legal position, and the register is not wrong merely because a fence stands elsewhere. The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, the decision on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The revision is not admitted, because the case raises no question of fundamental significance and the Senate applies settled principles (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO). The value in dispute corresponds to the plaintiff's interest in the strip, which the Senate, following the parties' concurring estimate, puts at 9,000 euros.

subject: Termination of a commercial lease for arrears: rent lawfully reduced for a defect is not rent in arrears
bears_on: case_mill page 1 (six months of arrears, 8,400 euros, termination sought; the tenant admits withholding and pleads a defect) and page 2 (the flooding record)
titelzeile: Termination of a commercial lease for arrears: rent lawfully reduced for a defect is not rent in arrears
leitsatz: Rent that is reduced by operation of law under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB because of a defect the landlord has not remedied is not owed and cannot be counted as rent in arrears for the purposes of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB. Before terminating for arrears the landlord must subtract the justified reduction; only the amount withheld above it is in default.

In a commercial lease no warning is required before a termination without notice for arrears (§ 543 Abs. 3 Satz 2 Nr. 3 BGB); whether the termination is effective depends solely on whether the excess withheld above the justified reduction reaches the thresholds of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB.
tenor: On the defendant's appeal the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 17 February 2009 – 2 O 188/08 – is amended and restated as follows.

The defendant is ordered to pay the plaintiff 1,980 euros with interest of five percentage points above the base rate from 3 June 2008. The further claim, in particular the claim for eviction and return of the hall, is dismissed.
The further appeal of the defendant is dismissed. Of the costs of the proceedings in both instances the plaintiff bears nine tenths and the defendant one tenth.

tatbestand.text: The parties dispute the eviction from, and the rent of, a commercial hall. By written lease of 12 March 2005 the plaintiff let to the defendant, a joinery, a workshop hall with an adjoining storage annex on the plaintiff's yard at the edge of Grevenau for ten years at a monthly rent of 1,100 euros, payable in advance. The annex, roughly two fifths of the let area, served the defendant as its timber store. The yard drains through a gully in front of the annex into a culvert on the plaintiff's premises.

From November 2007 water entered the annex after heavy rain. The defendant reported this to the plaintiff in writing on 14 November 2007 and repeatedly thereafter. Its log, with photographs, records seven ingresses up to April 2008, each time because the gully was blocked and surface water backed up over the sill; timber stored in the annex warped. The plaintiff promised to have the culvert cleared but did not. From December 2007 the defendant paid no rent. By letter of 2 June 2008 the plaintiff terminated the lease without notice for six months' arrears, December 2007 to May 2008, in the amount of 6,600 euros, and demanded the return of the hall.

The plaintiff has claimed eviction and payment of 6,600 euros with interest at five percentage points above the base rate from 3 June 2008. The defendant has admitted withholding the rent and contended that the rent was reduced to nil because the hall was unusable. The Landgericht Grevenau, by judgment of 17 February 2009, granted the claim in full. It held that the defendant had withheld the entire rent, that only the annex was affected, that any reduction plainly fell far short of the whole, and that the arrears therefore exceeded two months' rent whatever the reduction came to; it did not measure the reduction. With its appeal the defendant pursues the dismissal of the claim. The plaintiff defends the judgment.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in time and in the proper form (§§ 511, 517, 519, 520 ZPO). It is founded in part. The termination of 2 June 2008 did not end the lease, so that the claim for eviction fails. The claim for payment succeeds only in the amount by which the rent withheld exceeds the reduction to which the defendant was entitled.
II.

A landlord may terminate without notice where the tenant is in default with the rent or a not insignificant part of it on two consecutive dates, or over a period extending over more than two dates with an amount reaching two months' rent (§ 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB). In a commercial lease no prior warning is needed; § 543 Abs. 3 Satz 2 Nr. 3 BGB dispenses with it for this ground of termination. So far the Senate agrees with the Landgericht. The question is what counts as rent in arrears.

Rent is in arrears only insofar as it is owed. Under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB, where the let premises have a defect that removes or diminishes their fitness for the contractual use, the rent is remitted while the fitness is removed and appropriately reduced while it is diminished. The reduction takes effect by operation of law; it needs no declaration by the tenant and no consent of the landlord. A tenant who withholds no more than the justified reduction pays what is due and is not in default. The Landgericht was wrong to leave the reduction unmeasured because the defendant withheld everything. The landlord must first subtract the justified reduction from the rent withheld; only the remainder is default and is measured against the thresholds of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB.

The hall was defective throughout the six months. Under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB the plaintiff must keep the premises fit for the contractual use; a yard drainage that sends surface water over the sill of a timber store at every heavy rain does not meet that duty, and fault does not matter for the reduction. On the defendant's log and photographs, not disputed in substance, the annex was flooded seven times and stayed damp in between, and could not serve as a timber store. The workshop remained usable, but around each ingress the defendant had to raise its machines and stock. The Senate values the reduction at 70 per cent: the annex, two fifths of the rental value, was wholly unusable; the workshop, three fifths, was diminished by half.

Accordingly, of the monthly rent of 1,100 euros the defendant owed 330 euros for each of the six months and withheld 1,980 euros above the justified reduction. With that excess it was in default, since it relied on no right of retention but withheld the rent on the footing that nothing was owed. The excess does not reach the thresholds of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB. For two consecutive dates it comes to 660 euros, which is no not insignificant part of the rent, since in a commercial lease that requires more than one month's rent; over the whole period it comes to 1,980 euros, short of two months' rent of 2,200 euros. The termination was therefore ineffective and the claim for eviction is unfounded.
III.

The claim for payment is founded in the amount of 1,980 euros. The defendant owed the reduced rent of 330 euros for each of the six months and has not paid it; it was in default with each instalment from its due date (§ 286 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 BGB), and the interest claimed from 3 June 2008 is owed (§ 288 Abs. 1 BGB). The further claim is unfounded. Costs follow from § 92 Abs. 1 ZPO, provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. There is no ground to admit an appeal on a point of law (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO).

titelzeile: Irrigation ditch on the neighbour's parcel: accession, and no compensation without an increase in value
tenor: The action is dismissed. On the counterclaim, the plaintiff is ordered to tolerate the filling by the defendant of the irrigation ditch that runs along the western side of the wire fence on parcel 87/2 of the Grevenau land registry.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff operates a fruit plantation on parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry; the defendant farms the adjoining parcel 87/2 to the east. A wire fence has stood between them since before 1980. In the spring of 1994 the plaintiff, taking the fence for the boundary, excavated an irrigation ditch 1.2 metres wide and 160 metres long west of the fence, shored its banks with timber, set a sluice board into its northern end and fed it from the drainage channel that runs to the Greven creek. Since then the ditch has supplied the plantation's drip lines. A survey by the public surveyor, commissioned by the defendant in October 2008, placed the fence 2.9 metres west of the registered boundary; the ditch therefore lies entirely within parcel 87/2. The plaintiff does not contest the measurement.

In March 2009 the defendant gave notice that he would fill the ditch and plough the strip. The plaintiff objected and has declared that he will oppose any filling. He contends that he built the ditch in good faith and at his own expense, which he puts at 14,800 euros, that it is his work and remains his to keep and use, and that the defendant, who now holds a drained and serviced strip, must in any event pay for it. He seeks a declaration that he is entitled to maintain and use the ditch, an order that the defendant refrain from filling it and, in the alternative, payment of 14,800 euros with interest.

The defendant asks that the action be dismissed and, by way of counterclaim, that the plaintiff be ordered to tolerate the filling of the ditch. He argues that whatever lies in his soil is his, that the ditch serves nobody but the plaintiff and withdraws some 190 square metres from his cultivation, and that the plaintiff, who has drawn water across his land for fifteen years without asking, owes him rather than the reverse. The chamber has heard the surveyor as a witness and obtained a written opinion of an agricultural expert on the effect of the ditch on the value of parcel 87/2; reference is made to the opinion of 2 July 2010.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The action is admissible. The plaintiff has the interest required by § 256 Abs. 1 ZPO in a declaration of the right he asserts, since the defendant disputes it and has announced that he will act against it. The counterclaim is admissible under § 33 ZPO; it arises from the same facts. The action is, however, unfounded in each of its applications, and the counterclaim is well founded.
II.

The plaintiff is not the owner of the ditch. Its bed and banks are cut from the soil of parcel 87/2, and the timber shoring and the sluice board that the plaintiff brought onto the strip are joined with the ground so firmly that they cannot be separated without being destroyed. They are essential components of the parcel under § 94 Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB, and under § 946 BGB the ownership of the parcel extends to them. That parcel is the defendant's: the boundary runs where the register and the surveyor's plan put it, not where the fence has stood (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08). § 946 BGB does not ask who effected the joining or in what belief; cost and good faith bear on compensation, not on ownership.

Nor has the plaintiff a right to keep and use the ditch that could stand against the defendant's ownership. A right to use a neighbour's land arises only from a servitude registered under §§ 873, 1018 BGB or from an agreement; there is neither. Fifteen years of unobjected use give no title. The defendant may therefore deal with the ditch as he pleases and fill it (§ 903 Satz 1 BGB), and the plaintiff, who continues to draw water through it and has declared that he will oppose the filling, must tolerate it, since he has no right that would oblige the defendant to leave the ditch open (§ 1004 Abs. 1 and 2 BGB). The counterclaim is well founded, and the applications for a declaration and for an injunction fail.

The plaintiff is not entitled to compensation either. Whoever loses a right under § 946 BGB may demand compensation in money under the provisions on unjust enrichment (§ 951 Abs. 1 Satz 1, § 812 Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB). The measure of that claim is not what the loser spent but what the owner gained: the amount by which the parcel is worth more with the thing than without it. There is no such gain here. The expert, whom the chamber follows, found that an open ditch carrying water only to the plaintiff's drip lines is of no use to the cultivation of parcel 87/2, withdraws some 190 square metres from it and must be kept clear or filled at the owner's cost. The plaintiff's outlay served his own plantation; it is not the defendant's enrichment.
III.

The decision on costs rests on § 91 Abs. 1 Satz 1 ZPO. The plaintiff has been unsuccessful with the action in each of its applications and on the counterclaim, so that the costs of both fall to him. The decision on provisional enforceability follows from § 709 Satz 1 and Satz 2 ZPO; the security for the order to tolerate has been measured by the loss the plaintiff would suffer if the ditch were filled and the judgment later set aside.

subject: A public surveyor's plan of the registered boundary is a public document: what it proves and what does not contest it
bears_on: case_orchard page 2 (a jointly commissioned survey by the public surveyor Lena Ortiz; the claimant does not contest the measurement)
titelzeile: Public surveyor's boundary plan as a public document; the fence objection does not contest the measurement
tenor: The immediate complaint of the applicant against the order of the Landgericht Grevenau, 2. Zivilkammer, of 3 February 2011 – 2 OH 4/11 – is dismissed.
The applicant bears the costs of the complaint proceedings, including the costs incurred by the respondent in them.
The value in dispute for the complaint proceedings is fixed at 6,000 euros, corresponding to the value of the strip as assessed by the chamber.

gruende.text: The applicant, the market gardener K., is the registered owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry. The respondent, a farming partnership of the family Mertens, owns the adjoining parcel 87/2 to the east. Between the two parcels runs an old wire fence of some 140 metres, which according to the applicant has stood in its present line since 1974. On the joint instruction of both parties the publicly appointed surveyor S. located the registered boundary in the summer of 2010. His plan of 14 September 2010 places the fence, over its whole length, 2.6 metres east of the registered boundary line, that is inside parcel 87/2. The strip between the line and the fence, which the applicant uses as the access path to his glasshouses, therefore belongs by the geometry of the register to parcel 87/2.

The applicant thereupon applied to the Landgericht for the independent taking of evidence under § 485 Abs. 2 ZPO seeking a court-appointed expert's opinion on the true course of the boundary. He submitted that the measurement of the surveyor S., which he did not contest as such, could not decide where the boundary lay, because the fence had marked it for more than thirty years. The chamber rejected the application by order of 3 February 2011 without an oral hearing. The applicant's immediate complaint of 14 February 2011, which the chamber did not remedy, is admissible under § 567 Abs. 1 Nr. 2, § 569 ZPO: the order rejects an application concerning the procedure without an oral hearing, and in the independent taking of evidence that rejection ends the matter for the applicant. The complaint is unfounded.

The chamber rightly refused the opinion sought: the applicant lacks the legal interest § 485 Abs. 2 Satz 2 ZPO requires. A finding that the line lies where a public document already fully proves it to lie cannot serve to avoid a dispute; the only dispute left between these parties is one of law. The plan of a publicly appointed surveyor locating the registered boundary is a public document within § 418 Abs. 1 ZPO: he certifies within his public office a fact he has himself established in the terrain. It fully proves that the registered line runs 2.6 metres west of the fence. The land register describes the parcels by reference to the cadastre (§ 2 Abs. 2 GBO); the ownership presumed for the respondent under § 891 BGB is therefore ownership of parcel 87/2 as the cadastre bounds it, and with it the strip.

It is immaterial that the survey was commissioned by the parties jointly and not ordered by a court. § 418 ZPO asks who drew up the document and in what capacity, not who instructed or paid for it; a plan that the surveyor drew up in the exercise of his public office loses nothing of its evidential force because both neighbours asked for it. Counter-proof remains open under § 418 Abs. 2 ZPO, but it must be directed against the certified fact. A party who wishes to displace the plan must show that the measurement is wrong: that the surveyor started from the wrong cadastral points, misread the geometry of the register, or erred in the field. The applicant offers nothing of the kind. He expressly accepts the measurement and disputes only its consequence.

The objection that the fence has always stood where it stands does not contest the measurement. It says where the parties and their predecessors have fenced, cultivated and walked; it concerns possession and use, not the line. The Senate has already held that a boundary lies where the register and the survey put it, not where a fence has stood (judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08). Whether decades of use beyond the line give the applicant a right against the respondent, or whether the respondent must tolerate the path, is a question of law to be decided in an action on the merits. It is not a fact on which an expert could report, and the independent taking of evidence under § 485 ZPO serves only the establishment of facts.

Nor does the prospect of a second survey give the application the interest it lacks. A court deciding the boundary forms its conviction under § 286 ZPO from the whole content of the proceedings; where the line is proven by a public document and the party bearing counter-proof does not contest the measurement, no further survey is owed. A second survey by another publicly appointed surveyor, working from the same cadastral data, would repeat the first rather than examine it. The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO. The value in dispute for the complaint proceedings corresponds to the value of the strip as the chamber assessed it (§ 3 ZPO).

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff owns the former tannery on the Greven creek and let its workshop hall with an adjoining store to the defendant, a joinery, by lease of 1 March 2008 for ten years at 2,100 euros a month. The plaintiff has no office there; it employs a caretaker, the witness W., who holds the keys, admits tradesmen and receives the tenants' complaints. From November 2009, whenever the creek ran high, water entered the store through a floor drain and stood among the defendant's timber. The defendant's foreman recorded each ingress in a book with date, depth and photographs, seven entries between 14 November 2009 and 9 February 2011, and handed each entry to the witness W., who countersigned and dated three of them. From December 2009 the defendant paid the rent reduced by 420 euros a month.

The plaintiff claims the difference for fifteen months, 6,300 euros with interest. It contends that it was never notified of any ingress before the defendant's letter of 2 March 2011, that the caretaker is a handyman without authority to receive declarations on its behalf, and that the defendant is therefore barred from reducing the rent under § 536c Abs. 2 Satz 2 Nr. 1 BGB. It disputes the dates in the book. The defendant asks that the action be dismissed. It maintains that every entry was handed to the caretaker within days, that the caretaker is the only person the plaintiff made available on site, and that the countersignatures speak for themselves. The chamber has heard the witness W. and the defendant's foreman, the witness D.; reference is made to the minutes of 5 July 2011.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The action is admissible but unfounded. The plaintiff has no claim to the withheld rent under § 535 Abs. 2 BGB, because for the period in dispute the rent was reduced by operation of law under § 536 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB. A store in which the tenant's timber stands in water whenever the creek is high is not fit for the use the lease provides; the plaintiff does not seriously dispute that water entered, only that it knew. The measure of the reduction, one fifth of the rent, corresponds to the share of the premises affected and is not contested. Rent that is lawfully reduced never falls due and cannot be in arrears (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09). Whether the reduction stands therefore turns on § 536c BGB alone.
II.

The defendant gave notice of the defect and is therefore not barred under § 536c Abs. 2 Satz 2 Nr. 1 BGB. The duty under § 536c Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB is bound to no form. It is met by any communication that reaches the landlord and tells him what is wrong, where and since when, so that he can remedy it. A dated written record of each ingress, with its depth and photographs, handed over within days of the event, says more than the statute asks; the plaintiff could not have wished for a better notice. Its objection is not that the record said too little but that it was handed to the wrong person. The chamber does not follow this.

A notice of a defect is a communication of fact, not a declaration of intent. What matters is not who may bind the landlord but whose knowledge counts as his, and that is answered by § 166 Abs. 1 BGB by analogy: whoever entrusts another with a sphere of duties in which that person is to receive information and pass it on must accept that person's knowledge as his own. The plaintiff placed the witness W. in charge of the building. He holds the keys, admits tradesmen and receives the tenants' complaints; there is no one else on site. A landlord who organises his building so that the tenants deal with the caretaker makes the caretaker his agent for receiving their notices about its condition. He cannot afterwards say that what reached the caretaker did not reach him.

The chamber is convinced (§ 286 ZPO) that the entries reached the witness W. Three bear his signature and date; he confirmed the signature as his and could not recall ever refusing a sheet. The witness D. described the practice consistently: the sheet was written on the day and taken to the caretaker's lodge the next morning. The dates in the book match the photographs and the creek gauge readings the plaintiff itself submitted. The countersignatures prove receipt of those three entries. They also make the remaining four credible: same book, same hand, same practice, and the plaintiff offers no reason why the witness D. should have recorded three floods faithfully and invented four. That nothing appears in the plaintiff's files shows only that the caretaker did not pass the sheets on, which is the plaintiff's sphere.

Even if the four uncountersigned entries had not been handed over, nothing would follow. Under § 536c Abs. 2 Satz 2 BGB the tenant loses the rights under § 536 BGB only insofar as the landlord, because the notice was omitted, could not remedy the defect. The provision is not a penalty for incomplete paperwork; it withholds from the tenant what the landlord lost by not being told, and no more. From the first countersigned entry of 14 November 2009 the plaintiff knew that water entered the store whenever the creek ran high. Every later ingress was the same defect at the same drain; a further sheet would have told the plaintiff nothing it did not already know. The plaintiff lost nothing by any omission, and the reduction stands for the whole period.
III.

The decision on costs rests on § 91 Abs. 1 Satz 1 ZPO; the plaintiff has been unsuccessful in full, and the costs of the taking of evidence form part of the costs of the proceedings. The decision on provisional enforceability follows from § 708 Nr. 11 and § 711 ZPO. The value in dispute is set at 6,300 euros (§ 3 ZPO), the amount of the withheld rent claimed.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff demands the part of the rent that the defendant withheld because water entered the storage annex of the leased premises. By a lease of 14 February 2008 the plaintiff let to the defendant, which runs a joinery, the production hall of the former dye works on parcel 41/6 of the Grevenau land registry, sixty metres from the Greven creek, with a single-storey storage annex on the creek side, for ten years from 1 March 2008 at a monthly rent of 2,400 euros. The hall measures 600 square metres, the annex 200; under § 2 of the lease the annex serves for the storage of materials and finished goods.

Between 27 November 2009 and 19 February 2011 water entered the annex seven times, each within two days of heavy rainfall, through the floor slab and beneath the sill of the rear door, and stood up to twelve centimetres deep. The defendant recorded each event with photographs in a log and notified the plaintiff of the first by letter of 30 November 2009. According to the log, whose dates the plaintiff does not dispute, the annex could not be used on 41 days in all, drying days included; twice veneer stored there was spoiled. From December 2009 the defendant paid the rent reduced by 20 per cent.

The plaintiff has claimed the difference for December 2009 to March 2011, 7,680 euros, with interest at five percentage points above the base rate since 1 April 2011. It has contended that the water came from an overloaded municipal storm drain beyond its control, that it was not at fault, and that the defendant, never having declared a reduction, had simply fallen into arrears. The Landgericht Grevenau, by judgment of 4 October 2011 – 7 O 19/11 –, dismissed the action: the annex had been practically worthless for storage throughout, and a reduction of 20 per cent was in any event appropriate. With its appeal the plaintiff pursues the claim in full; the defendant defends the judgment.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible (§§ 511, 517, 520 ZPO). On the merits it succeeds only in part. The defendant was entitled to pay a reduced rent, because the annex was defective from the first ingress (§ 536 Abs. 1 BGB) and the reduction took effect by operation of law without any declaration. The Landgericht, however, measured the reduction too generously: on the Senate's estimate under § 287 ZPO the rent for the period in dispute was reduced by 2,570 euros in all, so that the defendant still owes 5,110 euros of the 7,680 euros withheld.
II.

The annex was defective within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB. A defect is any deviation of the actual from the contractual condition that impairs fitness for the agreed use. The lease designates the annex for storage, and a storage room into which water repeatedly enters and stands on the floor is not fit for that use. The defect existed from the first ingress on 27 November 2009. What appeared that day was not an isolated accident but the condition of the building, as the six further events confirmed; a room that floods after heavy rain is unfit for storage from the day it first does so, not from the day the parties accept that it will happen again.

Where the water came from is immaterial, and so is fault. The plaintiff's reliance on an overloaded municipal storm drain beyond its control misses the point of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB. The reduction is not a sanction for a breach of duty but the consequence of the object not being in the condition that § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB obliges the landlord to maintain throughout the term. Whether the landlord could have prevented the deviation, and whether it is to blame for it, matters for damages under § 536a Abs. 1 BGB, which are not claimed here. Nor does it help the plaintiff that the annex stayed dry before 2009: the duty to maintain is continuing, not discharged by delivery.

The reduction did not depend on any declaration by the defendant. Under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB the tenant, while fitness is impaired, owes only an appropriately reduced rent; the reduction operates by law, and a tenant who pays the reduced amount pays what is owed, not less. The plaintiff confuses the reduction with the duty of notice under § 536c Abs. 1 BGB, which the defendant in any event performed by its letter of 30 November 2009. As the Senate has held, rent lawfully reduced for a defect is not rent in arrears (judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09); the defendant therefore did not fall into default for want of a declaration.

The measure of the reduction is the impairment of the use of the leased object as a whole, taken against the whole rent and estimated under § 287 ZPO. The Landgericht rightly started from the annex's share of the floor area. The lease sets a single rent for hall and annex, and neither party has shown that its value for the defendant's business departs from its share of area; the Senate therefore takes the annex as one quarter of the leased object. On the days on which water stood in the annex or it was drying, 41 days on the uncontested log, the annex was wholly unusable while the hall remained in use. For those days the rent was reduced by 25 per cent.

Between the events the annex was usable, but not as the lease promised. A tenant who has seen water stand twelve centimetres deep cannot store veneer or finished pieces there as before; the defendant had to keep goods raised and clear the annex whenever heavy rain was forecast. That standing risk over the stored goods is itself an impairment of use, estimated at 5 per cent of the whole rent. For the 486 days from 1 December 2009 to 31 March 2011, at a daily rent of 79.01 euros, this yields about 810 euros for the 41 flood days and about 1,758 euros for the remaining 445 days, together 2,570 euros in round figures. The Landgericht's flat 20 per cent, which treats the annex as worthless throughout, overstates this.
III.

The defendant therefore owes 5,110 euros. Interest is due from 1 April 2011 as claimed, the rent for every month in dispute having fallen due by then (§ 286 Abs. 2 Nr. 1, § 288 Abs. 1 BGB). The decision on costs follows from § 92 Abs. 1 ZPO, the plaintiff prevailing as to two thirds of its claim; that on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The revision is not admitted, the case having no fundamental significance (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO).

norm: § 900 Abs. 1 BGB, § 927 BGB, § 891 BGB, § 985 BGB
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 6. Januar 2012, Az: 2 O 270/12, Urteil
subject: Thirty years of possession beyond the fence acquire no title: acquisitive prescription needs thirty years of registration, not of use
bears_on: case_orchard page 2 (the claimant argues the fence has stood since at least 1996 and the strip's use has been exclusively its own) and page 3 (the witness on the fence and the ditch)
titelzeile: Acquisitive prescription: thirty years of registration, not thirty years of cultivation beyond the fence
leitsatz: A strip lying within a neighbour's registered parcel is not acquired by thirty years of exclusive cultivation beyond the fence. Acquisition by prescription under § 900 Abs. 1 BGB presupposes that the possessor has been registered as owner of the land for thirty years; proprietary possession alone, however long, confers no title.

The neighbour's tolerance of the use, however long, is neither a transfer of ownership nor the ground of a presumption against the register (§ 891 BGB). Exclusive use founds at most the protection of possession, not a right to possess against the registered owner's claim under § 985 BGB.
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau, 2. Zivilkammer, of 25 August 2011 – 2 O 88/10 – is dismissed.
The plaintiff bears the costs of the appeal proceedings; the decision of the Landgericht on the costs of the first instance remains unaffected.

This judgment and the judgment under appeal are provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by security of 110 per cent of the enforceable amount unless the defendant first gives security in the same amount.
The revision is not admitted. The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set at 9,500 euros.

tatbestand.text: The parties are neighbouring farmers and dispute a strip of land along their common boundary. The plaintiff is the registered owner of parcel 61/2 of the Grevenau land registry, taken over from his father in 1994. The defendant has been the registered owner of the adjoining parcel 61/3 to the south since 2009, when he bought it from the heirs of the farmer W. Between the fields runs a post-and-wire fence erected by the plaintiff's father in 1978. The strip of 3.9 metres by 210 metres north of that fence has been ploughed and cropped with parcel 61/2 by the plaintiff's family ever since; in 1985 the father also laid a field drain along it.

In 2010 the defendant had the boundary surveyed by a public surveyor. The plan places the fence 3.9 metres north of the registered boundary line, so that the strip lies, by the geometry of the register, within parcel 61/3. The plaintiff does not contest the measurement. He contends that ownership of the strip passed to his family through more than thirty years of exclusive cultivation and that the farmer W. and his heirs, by never objecting, accepted the fence as the boundary. He sought a declaration that he owns the strip and an order that the defendant refrain from entering it; the defendant counterclaimed for surrender of the strip and removal of the fence.

By judgment of 25 August 2011 – 2 O 88/10 – the Landgericht Grevenau dismissed the action and allowed the counterclaim. It held that the presumption of § 891 BGB stands for the defendant, that the plaintiff's evidence concerned use and not the register, and that § 900 Abs. 1 BGB fails for want of any registration of the plaintiff for the strip. On appeal the plaintiff pursues his claims and resists the counterclaim. He submits that § 900 BGB is aimed at anyone who has held land as his own for thirty years and that the tolerance by the previous owners must be treated as a transfer or shift the burden of proof. The defendant defends the judgment.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in due form and time. It is, however, unfounded. The Landgericht rightly dismissed the action and rightly allowed the counterclaim. The plaintiff is not the owner of the strip, and he has no right to possess it that he could set against the defendant.
II.

The defendant is the owner of the strip. He is registered for parcel 61/3, of which the strip forms part. The plan of the public surveyor proves where the registered line runs until its correctness is disproved (Senate, order of 22 March 2011 – 4 W 9/11). The presumption of § 891 Abs. 1 BGB therefore stands for the defendant, and it is not shaken by evidence of who ploughed the strip, how long the fence has stood or what was dug or laid beneath it. A boundary lies where the register and the survey put it, not where a fence stands (Senate, judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08).

The plaintiff has not acquired the strip under § 900 Abs. 1 BGB. The provision does not reward possession; it heals a wrong registration. Whoever is registered as owner of a parcel without having acquired ownership becomes owner if the registration has stood for thirty years and he has held the parcel in proprietary possession throughout. Both elements must coincide: thirty years in the book and thirty years on the land. The plaintiff and his father were registered for parcel 61/2 only, and that entry never extended to any part of parcel 61/3. Thirty years of use beyond the fence therefore amount, as to ownership, to nothing.

Nothing else follows from § 927 BGB, the only provision under which thirty years of proprietary possession count by themselves. Even there the possessor may only have the owner excluded by public notice proceedings, and where the owner is registered only if he is dead or missing and no entry requiring his consent has been made for thirty years. The farmer W. was alive and registered until his death, his heirs were registered after him, and the sale to the defendant in 2009 was duly entered. The legislature has thus answered the plaintiff's question: possession alone leads to title only by that procedure, and only where the register has fallen silent.

The tolerance of the fence and of the cultivation by the farmer W. and his heirs is no transfer of ownership. Ownership of land passes by agreement and registration (§§ 873, 925 BGB); a neighbour who lets the adjoining farmer plough beyond the line declares nothing. Nor does long tolerance found a presumption against the register: § 891 BGB is rebutted by proof that the register is wrong, not by proof that the land was used as though it were. The plaintiff's central submission, taken from the appeal brief, reads as follows.

A family that has ploughed, sown and harvested a strip for more than thirty years, in full view of the neighbour and without objection, has made that land its own; possession this long must count for something, and the law cannot mean that a line on a plan nobody looked at for a generation undoes it.

The Senate does not follow this. Possession this long counts for nothing as to title. What it gives the plaintiff is possessory protection under §§ 858 ff. BGB against interference by force, and it may give him claims for the field drain he laid on what turns out to be the defendant's land (compare Landgericht Grevenau, judgment of 3 November 2010 – 2 O 311/09). It gives him no right to possess under § 986 Abs. 1 BGB against the owner. The defendant's claim under § 985 BGB for surrender of the strip is therefore well founded, and with it the claim to removal of the fence (§ 1004 Abs. 1 BGB).
III.

The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, the decision on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The revision is not admitted; the case has no fundamental significance and the Senate departs from no decision of another court (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO). The value in dispute follows the Landgericht's unchallenged finding on the value of the strip.

subject: A registered right of way binds every later owner of the servient parcel and survives a corrected boundary
bears_on: case_orchard page 4 (easement deed no. 98-4417, registered 11 August 1998 against parcel 114/2 in favour of the owner of 114/3, for agricultural passage to the Greven creek across the ditch track; 'even if the claimant were to establish ownership of the strip, the recorded right of way would survive it')
titelzeile: Right of way: a registered easement binds later owners and survives a corrected boundary
leitsatz: A right of way registered as a Grunddienstbarkeit (§ 1018 BGB) encumbers the servient parcel as a unit of the land register and belongs to the respective owner of the dominant parcel; every later owner of either parcel takes its position without any act of transfer (§§ 873 Abs. 1, 1019 BGB).

A survey that relocates the recognised boundary neither extinguishes the easement nor makes its entry incorrect under § 894 BGB. The right runs where the deed places it; even a successful boundary claim over the strip on which the track lies leaves it in place.
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau, 2. Zivilkammer, of 15 January 2013 – 2 O 188/12 – is dismissed.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff has owned parcel 61/3 of the Grevenau land registry since 2007, bought from the market gardener K., and runs a tree nursery on it. The defendant, a farmer, acquired the adjoining parcel 61/4 to the east from the family Mertens in 2010. Along the common boundary a drainage ditch runs southward to the Greven creek; on its western side lies a farm track about 3.5 metres wide, the ditch track. A wire fence east of the ditch has stood since the 1970s and was treated by all previous owners as the boundary.

By deed no. 94-1130, registered on 3 March 1994 in section II of the register sheet for parcel 61/3, K. granted the respective owner of parcel 61/4 a right of way across the ditch track, in settlement of a dispute about the drainage of the Mertens fields into the ditch. Since then the owners of parcel 61/4, the Mertens family and later the defendant, have driven along the track to the creek with tractors several times a year.

In October 2011 the publicly appointed surveyor F. measured the boundary. His plan places the registered line 2.9 metres west of the fence, so that by the geometry of the register the ditch and the greater part of the track belong to parcel 61/4; only a strip about one metre wide and the landing at the creek bank remain within parcel 61/3. The plaintiff does not contest the measurement. In a separate action pending before the Landgericht he claims the strip up to the fence, relying on the age of the fence.

The plaintiff sought a declaration that the right of way registered against parcel 61/3 is extinct. He argued that the survey had deprived the right of its object, since the track now lay almost entirely on the defendant's own land; should the strip prove to be his, the right had lapsed, because it had been granted by K. to the Mertens family and both parcels had since changed hands. The Landgericht Grevenau, 2. Zivilkammer, dismissed the action by judgment of 15 January 2013 – 2 O 188/12. The plaintiff appeals; the defendant defends the judgment.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in time and in the proper form. So is the declaratory action: the plaintiff has the interest required by § 256 Abs. 1 ZPO, because the defendant relies on the registered right and continues to drive along the track, and a declaration would settle the dispute as completely as an action for consent to deletion.
II.

The appeal is unfounded. The right of way registered against parcel 61/3 exists and binds the plaintiff. A Grunddienstbarkeit is created by the agreement of the owner of the servient parcel with the person entitled and by registration (§ 873 Abs. 1 BGB). Both were met in 1994: K., then owner of parcel 61/3, agreed the encumbrance with the Mertens family, then owners of parcel 61/4, and the right was entered. Passage across the servient parcel for agricultural purposes is a use of that parcel in an individual respect and thus a permissible content under § 1018 BGB.

The change of owners on both sides has not affected the right. § 1018 BGB creates it not for the person who negotiated it but for the respective owner of another parcel. It encumbers the servient parcel whoever owns it and belongs to whoever owns the dominant parcel; both pass with the parcels without any act of transfer. § 1019 BGB requires only that the servitude offer an advantage for the use of the dominant parcel, as the passage to the creek does. The plaintiff's ignorance of the deed when he bought is irrelevant: a purchaser takes the parcel with every encumbrance the register shows, and reliance on a fence line is not reliance on the register.

The survey has not extinguished the right either. The boundary lies where the register and the survey put it, not where the fence stands (Senate, judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08), and the surveyor's plan proves the course of the registered line unless shown to be wrong (Senate, order of 22 March 2011 – 4 W 9/11). But the easement is not registered against a strip of a given width. It is registered against parcel 61/3 as a unit of the land register, and where the passage runs across that parcel is determined by the deed, which provides:

The owner of parcel 61/3 grants the respective owner of parcel 61/4 a right of way over parcel 61/3 for agricultural passage to the creek across the ditch track, with due regard for the plantings on either side.

The course of the right is thus fixed by its purpose, reaching the creek, and by its location, the ditch track; neither depends on where the registered boundary lies. Where the track lies within parcel 61/3 the defendant passes by virtue of the easement, where it lies within parcel 61/4 as owner. The survey has altered which part falls into which category, not the course of the right.

It follows that the outcome of the plaintiff's boundary action is without significance here. Should he establish that the strip up to the fence belongs to parcel 61/3, the whole width of the track would lie within the servient parcel and be subject to the right of way; a successful boundary claim enlarges the area of exercise, it does not extinguish the right. Should he fail, nothing changes. In neither case is the register incorrect within the meaning of § 894 BGB, for it shows a right that exists.

Nor does § 1026 BGB assist the plaintiff. The provision applies where the servient parcel is divided and confines the servitude to the parts on which it is exercised. A survey divides nothing; it records where a parcel has always ended. Even by analogy the burden would remain on the part of parcel 61/3 across which the track runs, which is precisely where the defendant drives.
III.

The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, the decision on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The Revision is not admitted, because the matter is of no fundamental significance and the Senate applies settled principles to an individual case (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO).

subject: A five-year commercial lease without the written form runs for an indefinite period, and what that does and does not change about termination for arrears
bears_on: case_mill page 1 (a five-year lease at 1,400 euros per month since 2021; termination sought for arrears)
tenor: The appeal of the defendant against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 27 August 2013 – 7 O 44/13 – is dismissed.
The defendant bears the costs of the appeal proceedings. The judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau referred to above is provisionally enforceable without provision of security.
The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set at 17,250 euros, of which 13,800 euros fall on the claim for surrender of the hall and 3,450 euros on the claim for payment.

gruende.text: The plaintiff lets a workshop hall on its premises at the former dairy in Grevenau. The defendant, who runs a joinery, took the hall over on 1 April 2010. The plaintiff's draft lease of 22 March 2010 provided for a term of five years and a rent of 1,150 euros per month; the defendant signed the draft and returned it, the plaintiff never signed it. The defendant paid the rent until February 2013 and nothing thereafter. By letter of 6 June 2013, received the following day, the plaintiff terminated the lease without notice for arrears and demanded the surrender of the hall. By judgment of 27 August 2013 – 7 O 44/13 – the Landgericht Grevenau ordered the defendant to vacate and surrender the hall and to pay 3,450 euros with interest.

With its appeal the defendant argues that the lease never observed the written form of § 550 BGB and therefore ran for an indefinite period from the outset; that a lease of that kind can be ended only with the statutory notice of § 580a Abs. 2 BGB; and that the arrears are for that reason without significance, because the plaintiff could have ended the lease on notice at any time and because the defendant, uncertain whether a lease existed at all, was entitled to hold the rent back until that question was settled. By order of 8 October 2013 the Senate informed the parties that it intended to dismiss the appeal under § 522 Abs. 2 ZPO. The defendant's submission of 29 October 2013 repeats the argument and gives no cause for a different assessment.

The appeal is to be dismissed by unanimous order under § 522 Abs. 2 Satz 1 ZPO. It manifestly has no prospect of success, the matter has no fundamental significance, neither the development of the law nor the consistency of case law requires a judgment, and an oral hearing is not required. Under § 550 Satz 1 BGB, which § 578 Abs. 1 and 2 BGB extends to commercial premises, a lease for longer than one year that is not concluded in written form is deemed concluded for an indefinite period. A draft signed by the tenant alone does not satisfy that form (§ 126 Abs. 2 BGB). The lease is not void for that reason: § 550 BGB displaces § 125 BGB and confines the consequence of the defect to the term. The Landgericht rightly so held.

The lease therefore exists on the terms the parties agreed, at 1,150 euros per month, with the single difference that its five-year term gives way to an indefinite one. What that changes is the ordinary termination: either party may end the lease with the statutory notice of § 580a Abs. 2 BGB, by the third working day of a calendar quarter to the end of the next calendar quarter, though under § 550 Satz 2 BGB not before one year has passed since the premises were handed over. What it does not change is the tenant's obligation to pay the agreed rent for every month of use. A tenant who holds the premises under a lease that the law itself declares to run for an indefinite period owes the rent for as long as he holds them.

Nor does the missing form touch the right of either party to terminate the lease without notice for cause under § 543 Abs. 1 BGB. That right applies to leases for a definite and an indefinite period alike and is not displaced because the lease could also have been ended by ordinary notice. The two rights stand side by side; the landlord chooses, and is not to be kept bound to a tenant who pays nothing. The conditions of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB are therefore judged on their own, without regard to the form of the lease: whether the tenant was in default on two consecutive dates with the rent or a not insignificant part of it, or over more than two dates with an amount that reaches two months' rent.

Those conditions were met on 7 June 2013, when the termination arrived: the rent for March, April and May 2013 was unpaid, three consecutive dates and three months' rent. The default was not excused (§ 286 Abs. 4 BGB). The defendant's belief that no lease existed is an error of law; a tenant who uses the hall and knows the agreed rent could not hold it with due care, § 550 BGB being unambiguous. No defect and no reduction under § 536 BGB is pleaded, so rent lawfully reduced, which is not arrears (Senate, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09), is not in question. The defendant did not pay before the termination arrived (§ 543 Abs. 2 Satz 2 BGB), and the later cure of § 569 Abs. 3 Nr. 2 BGB is confined to residential leases.

The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO. The judgment of the Landgericht is provisionally enforceable without provision of security under §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 and 713 ZPO, since at the value in dispute no remedy lies against this order. That value is set at 17,250 euros: the claim for surrender of the hall is valued at one year's rent, 13,800 euros, the claim for payment at the 3,450 euros demanded.

subject: No way of necessity where a registered right of way already provides the access
bears_on: case_orchard page 4 (the deed grants passage to the Greven creek across the ditch track) and page 1 (the respondent crosses the strip with machinery)
tenor: The immediate complaint of the applicant against the order of the Landgericht Grevenau of 3 December 2013 – 2 O 402/13 – is dismissed.
The applicant bears the costs of the complaint proceedings, including the costs incurred by the respondent in the proceedings before the Senate.
The value in dispute of the complaint proceedings is set at 5,000 euros, in line with the value the Landgericht set for the application.

gruende.text: The applicant farms parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, a field of some four hectares which has been irrigated since the nineteen-nineties with water pumped from the Greven creek. Between the field and the creek lies parcel 87/2, which the respondent acquired in 2012. Until 2004 both parcels formed one parcel; on the partition a right of way was registered against parcel 87/2 in favour of the respective owner of parcel 87/1 for passage with agricultural vehicles to the Greven creek along the field track on the eastern edge. In October 2013 the respondent chained the track, declared that he needed it for drainage works, and offered the applicant in its place a passage along the northern headland of parcel 87/2 against an annual payment. The applicant refused the offer.

The applicant applied to the Landgericht for an interim order that the respondent tolerate passage to the creek across parcel 87/2 as a way of necessity under § 917 Abs. 1 BGB, the direction of the way to be determined by the court. He rested the application on § 917 BGB alone. In his view the field is without the connection its proper use requires for as long as the track is chained, and the respondent's own offer shows that a way of necessity against payment is the fitting form of access. The Landgericht refused the application by the order under complaint. The immediate complaint, lodged in time, is admissible under §§ 567 Abs. 1 Nr. 2, 569 ZPO. The Senate has heard the respondent. The complaint is unfounded.

A way of necessity under § 917 Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB presupposes that the parcel lacks the connection which its proper use requires. The provision applies correspondingly where the proper use of a field requires access to the watercourse from which it is irrigated; the connection then owed is the passage to the water. The field does not lack that connection. By the registered easement parcel 87/1 holds exactly the passage the applicant asks the court to grant him: a right to cross parcel 87/2 with agricultural vehicles to reach the water.

That its owner is at present hindered in exercising the easement creates no lack of connection. It gives him a claim against the hindrance under § 1027 in conjunction with § 1004 Abs. 1 BGB, which he may secure by interim order. That claim, however, is not the one before the Senate: the applicant seeks a way of necessity whose route the court is to determine, not toleration of the exercise of the registered easement along the field track, and the Senate may not award what has not been applied for, § 308 Abs. 1 ZPO.

§ 917 BGB adds no second route beside the one the parties created and registered. That the track is longer than a straight line across the field, and soft in spring, does not alter this: the way of necessity is not the better way but a way where otherwise there would be none. Route and state of the track are questions of the content and exercise of the easement, §§ 1018, 1020 BGB. Nor does § 918 BGB assist the applicant. Its second paragraph presupposes that the alienation of a part cut the alienated or the retained part off from the connection; on the partition of 2004 the same instrument created the easement which preserves it, and the respondent took parcel 87/2 in 2012 subject to that easement. § 918 Abs. 1 BGB likewise has no application, since the connection was not removed by any act of the applicant.

The respondent's offer of a passage along the northern headland changes nothing. A registered right of way burdens the servient parcel with the content registered, § 1018 BGB, and binds every later owner, as the Senate held in its judgment of 4 June 2013 – 4 U 23/13. Whether the respondent could demand that the exercise be relocated under § 1023 BGB need not be decided; he has made no such claim, has shown no place equally suitable for the applicant, and offers the headland against an annual payment, whereas § 1023 puts the cost of a relocation on the servient owner. What he cannot do is set the easement aside by offering a way of necessity elsewhere. What he must tolerate is the crossing of the track with the applicant's machinery to the water. The application was rightly refused. The costs follow from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, the value in dispute from § 3 ZPO.

subject: A flood gate is the landlord's to keep working: a gate reported jammed is a defect from the report, and budgeting the repair for next year is no discharge
bears_on: case_mill page 3 (the annex's flood gate reported jammed in September 2024 by the caretaker, budgeted for repair in the 2025 plan, and not repaired)
titelzeile: Flood gate reported jammed: the landlord's maintenance duty and a repair deferred to the next budget year
leitsatz: The landlord's duty under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB to keep the leased object fit for the contractual use extends to the protective installations that serve the premises. Where a hall is let beside a watercourse, the flood gate that keeps high water out of it is such an installation, and it is the landlord's to keep working.

A protective installation reported as jammed by the landlord's own caretaker is defective from the day of the report, and the caretaker's knowledge is the landlord's. Entering the repair in the following year's maintenance plan discharges nothing; after a reasonable period the landlord is in default of the remedy and owes damages under § 536a Abs. 1 BGB beside the reduction under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB.
tenor: The appeal of the defendant against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 8 October 2013 – 7 O 88/12 – is dismissed.
The defendant bears the costs of the appeal proceedings, including the costs of the taking of evidence before the Senate.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. The defendant may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum enforceable, unless the plaintiff first provides security in the same amount.

The appeal on a point of law is not allowed; the case raises no question of fundamental significance, and neither the development of the law nor the securing of uniform adjudication requires a decision of the court of last instance.

tatbestand.text: The parties are in dispute over rent and over damage caused by water entering a storage annex. By a written lease of 2009 the defendant let to the plaintiff, a joinery, the storage hall on parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, which stands some twenty metres from the Greven creek, at a rent of 2,100 euros a month. The annex of the hall, in which the plaintiff seasons timber, is protected against high water by a flood gate set into its outer wall. The defendant had the gate built in when the hall was converted in 2004, and the defendant's caretaker operates it.

On 14 July 2011 the defendant's caretaker, the witness S., recorded in the defendant's maintenance file that the lower runner of the gate was bent and that the gate could no longer be closed by hand. The defendant entered the repair in its maintenance plan for the year 2012 and did not carry it out. Between November 2011 and February 2012 water from the creek entered the annex on four occasions, each time within two days of the gauge at the mill weir exceeding 1.8 metres. Seasoned timber invoiced at 6,400 euros was spoiled. The plaintiff notified each entry of water in writing.

The plaintiff paid the rent in full until February 2012 and retained thirty per cent of it from March 2012 onwards. It has claimed repayment of 2,520 euros for the four months of ingress and damages of 6,400 euros; the defendant has counterclaimed for the 2,520 euros retained. The defendant has argued that high water is a natural event outside its sphere, that the gate remained serviceable if operated correctly, and that a repair provided for in the following budget year satisfies its duty. The Landgericht allowed the claim and dismissed the counterclaim. With its appeal the defendant pursues its motions of the first instance.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in due form and within the time allowed. It has no success in the matter. The Landgericht rightly held that the annex was defective within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB from 14 July 2011 onwards, that the defendant fell into default of the remedy it owed, that it is therefore liable in damages under § 536a Abs. 1 BGB, and that the part of the rent retained from March 2012 was not owed.
II.

Under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB the landlord must keep the leased object, for the whole of the lease, in a condition fit for the contractual use. That duty is not confined to the walls and the roof. It extends to the installations that serve the premises and shield them from the influences to which the site is exposed. Where a hall beside a watercourse is let for the storage of goods sensitive to moisture, the flood gate that keeps the water out is such an installation. It is the landlord's to keep working, and the tenant owes no maintenance of what the landlord built into the structure.

The gate was defective from 14 July 2011. A protective installation reported as jammed is unfit for its purpose from the day of the report; the defect does not first arise with the water that later enters. The Senate has heard the witness S. again and has obtained an expert opinion on the runner, and both confirm the entry in the maintenance file. The knowledge of the caretaker who keeps that file and operates the gate is the defendant's own knowledge; a landlord who has its installations watched by an agent may not treat what the agent records as unknown to it (Landgericht Grevenau, judgment of 16 August 2011 – 7 O 61/11).

That the repair stood in the maintenance plan for 2012 discharges nothing. What § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB owes the tenant is a working object, not a place in a budget, and the landlord's internal planning cycle is no measure of the time the tenant must wait; a gate that can be set right in weeks is to be set right in weeks. After a reasonable period from the report, which the Senate assesses at six weeks, the defendant was in default of the remedy without any reminder being required, the balance of the interests dispensing with one (§ 286 Abs. 2 Nr. 4 BGB) in the face of the approaching high-water season; from the first written notification it was in default in any event (§ 286 Abs. 1 BGB).

The consequences follow. The reduction under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB arises by operation of law and without regard to fault (Senate, judgment of 24 April 2012 – 8 U 99/11); the rate of thirty per cent found for the four months in which the annex could not be used for seasoning is not open to objection, so that 2,520 euros were paid without legal cause and are to be repaid, and the rent retained from March 2012 was not owed, rent lawfully reduced being no rent in arrears (Senate, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09). The spoiled timber is a loss caused by the delayed remedy and is to be made good under § 536a Abs. 1 BGB in the amount of 6,400 euros proved by the invoices.
III.

The decision on the costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO; the defendant has been unsuccessful both with its defence and with its counterclaim, and the evidence taken before the Senate went to the condition of the gate, that is to the point on which it has lost. The decision on provisional enforceability follows from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The appeal on a point of law is not allowed, the requirements of § 543 Abs. 2 ZPO not being met; the extent of the duty of maintenance in the individual lease is a question of the particular case.

subject: Crossing a neighbour's strip with machinery: the crosser must prove a right, and years of 'a word first' are a revocable licence, not a servitude

titelzeile: Crossing a neighbour's strip with machinery: a licence asked for each time is revocable and founds no servitude
tenor: The defendant is ordered to cease crossing, with vehicles or agricultural machinery, the strip of grass roughly four metres wide along the northern edge of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry.
For each case of infringement of that order the defendant is threatened with an administrative fine of up to 250,000 euros or, in the alternative, administrative detention of up to six months.
The defendant bears the costs of the proceedings, including the costs of the taking of evidence.
