tatbestand.text: The plaintiff is the owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, on which he runs a market garden. The defendant, a farm of the family Mertens, works parcel 87/4, which adjoins parcel 87/1 to the north. Along the northern edge of parcel 87/1 there runs a strip of grass roughly four metres wide between an old hedge and the ploughed land; over it the defendant's tractors and trailers reach the farm's own fields and a meadow at the Greven creek. No easement is registered against parcel 87/1.

The plaintiff submits that the crossings have always taken place with his permission, asked for in each single case, and that until 2012 they numbered a handful in the year. Since the summer of 2012 the defendant has driven over the strip with a combine harvester and heavy trailers, several times a week during the harvest and without any prior word, and has broken down the edge of the drainage channel. By letter of 4 October 2012 the plaintiff withdrew every permission. He applies for an order that the defendant cease crossing the strip with vehicles or agricultural machinery.

The defendant applies for the action to be dismissed. It submits that the farm and its predecessors have crossed the strip for more than forty years, that nobody ever objected, and that a right of way has arisen from that practice which the plaintiff must respect; at the least, the plaintiff has forfeited any claim by his long silence. The chamber has taken evidence by hearing the witness S., who has farmed the neighbouring land since 1979 and stated that the defendant's machinery went over the strip a few times a year and that a word was always had with the owner beforehand.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The action is admissible and well founded. The plaintiff may demand under § 1004 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB that the defendant cease crossing the strip. Driving over another's land with vehicles impairs ownership otherwise than by dispossession, and under § 903 BGB the owner may exclude every other person from the use of his land. The risk of repetition follows from the crossings that have already occurred; the defendant asserts a right to them and has continued them after the withdrawal of 4 October 2012.
II.

The plaintiff is not obliged to tolerate the crossings, § 1004 Abs. 2 BGB. A duty to tolerate is an objection to the claim, and whoever crosses another's land must prove the right on which he does so. The owner does not have to prove that no such right exists; he would be required to prove a negative, and the law does not ask that of him. The defendant has produced no title, and neither the length of the practice nor its peaceful course supplies one.

A right of way over a neighbouring parcel is an easement and arises by agreement and entry in the land register, §§ 873 Abs. 1, 1018 BGB. The certified extract of 6 March 2013 shows no entry of that kind against parcel 87/1. Use, however long, does not take the place of the entry; the Oberlandesgericht Grevenau so held in its judgment of 11 September 2012 – 4 U 140/11 for possession carried on beyond a fence for thirty years. Conversely, a right which is registered binds every later owner of the burdened parcel, judgment of 4 June 2013 – 4 U 23/13. It is the register that decides, not the practice on the ground.

What the witness has described is a licence and nothing more. Permission asked for and given for each single crossing is a gratuitous accommodation which the owner may withdraw at any time and without giving reasons; it confers no right in rem, binds no successor in title, and grows into no easement by being repeated. That the defendant asked beforehand each time shows that both sides understood the passage as a favour and not as an entitlement. The accommodation ended with the letter of 4 October 2012.

The claim is not forfeited, § 242 BGB. Forfeiture requires more than the passage of time: there must be circumstances in which the other party could trust, and did arrange its affairs in the trust, that the right would no longer be asserted. That second element is missing. A party which asks for permission before each crossing knows that permission may be refused; the practice of asking is the opposite of a basis for such trust. Still less can years of announced and occasional crossings excuse crossings of another kind, made unannounced, with heavier machinery and week by week.
III.

The decision on costs follows from § 91 Abs. 1 ZPO, that on provisional enforceability from § 709 Satz 1 ZPO. The threat of administrative measures rests on § 890 Abs. 2 ZPO. In fixing it the chamber has had regard to the weight of the machinery used and to the fact that the defendant continued the crossings after the permission had been withdrawn, in the belief that it was entitled to them.

vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 4. Juli 2014, Az: 2 O 92/14, Urteil
subject: A fence three metres off the line is not a boundary installation: §§ 921, 922 BGB presume joint use only of what stands on the boundary
bears_on: case_orchard page 2 (the old wire fence 3.2 m west of the registered boundary along the full length of the strip)
titelzeile: A fence three metres inside one parcel is no boundary installation: §§ 921, 922 BGB and the registered line
leitsatz: The presumption of joint entitlement in § 921 BGB, and with it the duty to share the cost of maintenance under § 922 BGB, attaches only to an installation which serves both parcels and stands on the boundary between them. A fence set back within one parcel is, under § 94 Abs. 1 BGB, that owner's own structure; no presumption of joint use arises from it.

The position of such a fence proves nothing about the course of the boundary, which runs where the land register and the surveyor's plan place it (§ 891 BGB). The neighbour may neither demand its maintenance nor resist its removal nor rely on it as the line, however long both sides have treated it as one.
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau, 2. Zivilkammer, of 24 June 2014 – 2 O 96/13 – is dismissed.
The costs of the appeal proceedings are borne by the plaintiff; the decision on the costs of the first instance in the judgment under appeal remains unaffected.

This judgment and the judgment under appeal are provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum enforceable, unless the defendant first provides security in the same amount.
The revision is not admitted. The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set at 11,600 euros.

tatbestand.text: The parties are neighbouring farmers in the district of Grevenau. The plaintiff, the horticulturist P., is the registered owner of parcel 132/5 of the Grevenau land registry, on which he raises nursery stock; the defendant, the farm of the family Ohlert, is the registered owner of the adjoining arable parcel 132/6 to the south. Along the common frontage of some 240 metres runs a wire fence on wooden posts which, as is undisputed, was erected in 1986 by the father of the present proprietor of the defendant farm and has stood in the same line ever since. The plaintiff has mown the ground up to the fence and has for years stacked crates against its northern side.

In 2013 the defendant had the boundary between the parcels located by the publicly appointed surveyor N. His plan of 8 October 2013 places the fence, over its whole length, between 3.0 and 3.1 metres south of the registered boundary, so that the fence itself, and the strip of some 730 square metres between it and the registered line, lie within parcel 132/6. The plaintiff does not contest the measurement. The defendant thereupon announced that it would take the fence down and bring its arable land up to the registered line. The plaintiff answered that the fence was a common boundary installation which the defendant might neither remove nor allow to fall into decay.

The plaintiff sought a declaration that the boundary between the parcels runs along the line of the fence; further, an order that the defendant refrain from removing or moving it; and payment of 5,200 euros, being half of the quoted cost of renewing it. He relied on §§ 921, 922 BGB. The chamber dismissed the action. It held that the presumption of § 921 BGB attaches only to installations standing on the boundary, and that the register and the surveyor's plan, and not the fence, fix the line. With his appeal the plaintiff pursues all three claims. The defendant defends the judgment under appeal.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in due form and within the time limits of §§ 511, 517, 519, 520 ZPO. The declaratory claim is admissible as well. The defendant disputes the plaintiff's understanding of the boundary in words and by its conduct on the ground, so that the interest in a declaration required by § 256 Abs. 1 ZPO exists. On the merits, however, the appeal has no success. The chamber decided all three claims correctly, and it did so for the right reason.
II.

The declaration sought cannot be made. A parcel has the extent which the land register, through the cadastre to which its description refers, gives it, and the presumption of § 891 Abs. 1 BGB covers that extent. Where the registered line is in doubt on the ground, the plan of a publicly appointed surveyor establishes it, being a public document whose accuracy stands until the contrary is proved (Senate, order of 22 March 2011 – 4 W 9/11). The plan of 8 October 2013 is uncontested. A fence is evidence not of a boundary but of where posts were once driven; it neither moves the line nor proves it (Senate, judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08).

The claims founded on §§ 921, 922 BGB fail for a reason which precedes every question of use. Section 921 BGB presumes joint entitlement where two parcels are separated by a ridge, a wall, a hedge, a fence or another installation serving the advantage of both parcels. The provision requires two things, and it requires them together: the installation must serve both parcels, and it must stand between them, that is, on the boundary. The second requirement is no formality. The presumption of joint entitlement, and the regime of joint use and shared cost which § 922 BGB builds upon it, make sense only because such an installation occupies the soil of both owners, so that neither can deal with it without reaching into the land of the other.

Here the second requirement is not met. The fence stands, over its whole length, about three metres inside parcel 132/6; it touches the land of the plaintiff nowhere. Being firmly attached to the ground, it is an essential part of that parcel under § 94 Abs. 1 BGB and belongs to the defendant alone. From this everything follows. No presumption of joint entitlement arises, so the plaintiff can demand no contribution to the cost of renewal under § 922 sentence 2 BGB; and the prohibition of § 922 sentence 3 BGB, under which a boundary installation may not be removed or altered without the consent of the other, does not bind the defendant, who is free to take down its own fence on its own land.

The plaintiff's remaining arguments concern use, and use cannot supply what position denies. That the fence has separated the two holdings for nearly thirty years, that implements have been leaned against it from both sides and that the plaintiff has mown up to it says nothing about where it stands. Nor has that use given him any right to the strip behind it: land is acquired by lapse of time only under § 900 Abs. 1 BGB, which presumes thirty years of registration as owner, and the plaintiff has never been registered for a square metre of parcel 132/6 (Senate, judgment of 11 September 2012 – 4 U 140/11). What the defendant and its father tolerated was a licence revocable at will, and it has now been revoked.
III.

This outcome leaves the parties in no uncertainty: either of them may require the boundary marks to be set on the surveyed line under § 919 BGB, and nothing prevents them from agreeing upon a fence on that line, which would then be a boundary installation in the proper sense. The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, that on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The revision is not admitted (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO): the case turns on the wording of § 921 BGB and on principles settled in this Senate. The value in dispute reflects the plaintiff's interest in the strip and in the fence.

norm: § 3 ZPO, § 719 ZPO, § 707 ZPO
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 13. Februar 2015, Az: 2 O 129/15, Beschluss
subject: Value in dispute of a boundary action over a strip of land, and refusal of a stay of enforcement
bears_on: case_orchard page 1 (a strip of roughly 3.4 by 180 metres; the declaration and the injunction sought)
tenor: The application of the appellant to stay enforcement of the injunction pronounced by the Landgericht Grevenau on 9 September 2015 – 2 O 88/14 –, by which he was restrained from crossing the disputed strip with agricultural machinery, is refused (§§ 719 Abs. 1 Satz 1, 707 Abs. 1 Satz 1 ZPO). A stay presupposes that enforcement would bring the party a disadvantage not to be made good, and the appellant has shown none: he reaches the fields on the creek side over the made track of his own parcel, by a detour of some four hundred metres, and the additional expense of that detour is a money loss which the outcome of the appeal can restore to him.

Nor does the appeal offer the prospect of success which would justify a stay. The line between the parcels is proved by the plan of the publicly appointed surveyor, a public document within § 418 ZPO, and the appellant does not contest the measurement but only the conclusion drawn from it; against such a plan the assertion that a fence has long stood elsewhere is no counter-proof (Senate, order of 22 March 2011 – 4 W 9/11), and years of use beyond the line acquire no title (Senate, judgment of 11 September 2012 – 4 U 140/11). The costs of the application form part of the costs of the appeal proceedings and are not separately assessed.

The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set under § 3 ZPO at 11,100 euros. For the declaratory claim to the strip the Senate takes its market value: the strip measures some 594 square metres of orchard land, and at the price of 12 euros per square metre which the parties do not dispute for land of this quality in the district that gives 7,100 euros, rounded. For the injunction against crossings the Senate takes the interest of the respondent in undisturbed use, which it assesses at 4,000 euros, having regard to the number of crossings asserted and to the damage to the ditch track alleged with them.

The two claims are not to be added at their full amounts for the purpose of the security under § 709 ZPO, since the injunction protects the same strip whose ownership the declaration would settle; for the value in dispute, however, they concern different objects and are added (§ 5 ZPO). This order is not open to challenge (§ 574 Abs. 1 Satz 1 ZPO); the order on the value in dispute may be corrected by the Senate of its own motion within the period of § 63 Abs. 3 GKG.

subject: Goods spoiled by water after the landlord was told and delayed the repair: damages, and the tenant's own share
bears_on: case_mill page 2 (two deliveries of flour, invoiced at 1,150 and 730 euros, written off) and page 3 (the repair deferred)
titelzeile: Damages for goods spoiled by water: the landlord's default in repair, and the tenant's own share
tenor: The defendant is ordered to pay the plaintiff 3,266 euros together with interest at five percentage points above the base rate since 4 November 2015. The action is dismissed as to the remainder.
Of the costs of the proceedings the plaintiff bears 14 percent and the defendant 86 percent.
The judgment is provisionally enforceable against provision of security in the amount of 110 percent of the amount to be enforced in each case.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff trades in seed grain and animal feed. By written lease of 1 March 2011 it rented from the defendant the storage annex of the former grain store on parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, some sixty square metres of floor, at 620 euros a month. The annex lies below the level of the creek bank and is drained through a wall outlet fitted with a backflow flap. On 12 September 2014 the defendant's caretaker recorded in the maintenance file that the flap no longer closed. The plaintiff sent the defendant a copy of that note on 20 September 2014 and asked for the flap to be replaced before the winter.

Water entered the annex on five dates between November 2014 and June 2015, each within two days of the creek gauge at Grevenau exceeding 1.7 metres: on 21 November 2014, 12 January 2015, 18 March 2015, 30 April 2015 and 5 June 2015. The plaintiff kept a dated log of the ingresses, which the caretaker countersigned on three occasions. Two consignments stored on the annex floor were soaked and written off, a delivery of 10 January 2015 invoiced at 2,480 euros and a delivery of 2 June 2015 invoiced at 1,310 euros. The flap was replaced in August 2015. By letter of 20 October 2015 the plaintiff demanded 3,790 euros by 3 November 2015.

The plaintiff applies for an order that the defendant pay it 3,790 euros with interest. It submits that the defendant knew of the defect from September 2014, had promised in October 2014 to see to the flap before the winter, and then let three seasons pass. The defendant applies for dismissal. It submits that high water is a natural event for which no landlord answers, that it was in no way at fault, that the work had properly been placed in the maintenance budget of the following year, and that the plaintiff, once the annex had taken water repeatedly, ought to have stored elsewhere or at least raised its stock from the floor. The chamber has heard the caretaker and the witness Nolte, the plaintiff's warehouseman.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The action is admissible and well founded in the amount awarded. The plaintiff is entitled to damages under § 536a Abs. 1 BGB in its third alternative, the defendant having been in default in remedying a defect of the leased property. The annex was defective. A wall outlet whose backflow flap no longer closes admits creek water that a working flap would have held out, so that the defect is the flap and not the high water; the defendant's objection that it does not answer for the weather misses the point. Recurring ingress into a storage annex let for the keeping of goods withdraws the very use agreed. Whether the defendant was at fault in the flap failing is immaterial to this alternative of the provision.
II.

The defendant was in default. The plaintiff's letter of 20 September 2014, enclosing the caretaker's own note, brought the defect to the defendant's knowledge, and a dated log handed to the landlord's agent and countersigned by him is notice, as this chamber has held (judgment of 16 August 2011 – 7 O 61/11). A demand within § 286 Abs. 1 BGB requires no particular form, and once the period reasonable for so small a piece of work had run without result, the defendant was in default from the beginning of November 2014. Placing the work in the following year's budget is no discharge but the deferral itself (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14).

The loss consists in the value of the two consignments. The plaintiff has produced the suppliers' invoices, its write-off notes and photographs of the soaked sacks, and the witness Nolte has described how the grain was already fermenting when it was cleared out. On that basis the chamber is satisfied, and estimates under § 287 ZPO, that seed grain which has taken creek water is unsaleable and without residual value. The invoiced price is the proper measure: the plaintiff had paid it, and goods of that kind are replaced at the price of the day, which the defendant does not say was any lower. No deduction for use as feed falls to be made.

The plaintiff must, however, bear a share of the loss of the second consignment, § 254 Abs. 1 BGB. After the third ingress of 18 March 2015 it knew that the annex took water whenever the creek rose, and it knew from the defendant's own letters that nothing would be done before the summer. To place a fresh delivery on the annex floor in June 2015, when pallets and a raised rack stood unused in the adjoining hall, was to disregard a risk it had before its eyes. Weighed against the defendant's continuing default, which remains by far the heavier cause, that carelessness justifies reducing the second item by two fifths, to 786 euros.

For the first consignment no share falls on the plaintiff. When that delivery was stored, the annex had taken water once in four years of use, and the defendant had written on 2 October 2014 that the flap would be seen to before the winter; a tenant may act on such an assurance for a time. Nor does § 254 Abs. 1 BGB oblige a tenant to carry out the landlord's repair at its own cost, or to leave unused the space for which it pays rent. It requires only the care a reasonable person takes of its own goods. The claim is accordingly made out in the amount of 3,266 euros.
III.

Interest follows from §§ 286 Abs. 1, 288 Abs. 1 BGB, the letter of 20 October 2015 having set 3 November 2015 for payment, so that default began on the following day. As to the remaining 524 euros the action is dismissed. The decision on costs rests on § 92 Abs. 1 ZPO and follows the parties' shares in the outcome; provisional enforceability follows from § 709 Satz 1 and 2 ZPO.

vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 10. Juli 2015, Az: 2 O 203/15, Urteil
subject: What 'agricultural passage' allows: the scope of a right of way follows its purpose as farming develops, considerate exercise limits the manner, not the frequency
bears_on: case_orchard page 4 (the deed's purpose: agricultural passage to the Greven creek across the ditch track), page 3 (crossings became frequent and unannounced after 2018) and page 1 (the ditch and access track)
titelzeile: The scope of a right of way for agricultural passage: purpose, developing farming, and considerate exercise
leitsatz: The extent of a right of way follows from the entry in the land register and from the deed to which it refers, construed from its wording and its stated purpose (§ 1018 BGB, §§ 133, 157 BGB). A right granted for agricultural passage covers the passage which the farming of the dominant parcel requires as that farming develops.

The duty of considerate exercise under § 1020 BGB governs the manner of the passage, that is its route, its speed and the care owed to installations of the servient owner such as a ditch or a track. It does not cap the frequency. An announcement before each crossing is owed only where the deed provides for it.
tenor: On the appeal of the plaintiff the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 9 December 2015 – 2 O 355/15 – is amended: the defendant must cross parcel 87/1 only on the made track and must restore the ditch culvert.
In all other respects the appeal is dismissed, in particular in so far as it seeks to limit the crossings to twelve in each year and to require the announcement of each crossing on the previous day.
Of the costs of both instances the plaintiff bears four fifths and the defendant one fifth.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. Each party may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum to be enforced, unless the other party first provides security in like amount.

tatbestand.text: The parties own neighbouring parcels. The plaintiff is the owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, a meadow crossed from north to south by a made farm track running beside a drainage ditch. The defendant owns and farms parcel 87/3, which adjoins to the east and which reaches the fields on the creek side only over that track. A right of way in favour of the respective owner of parcel 87/3 has been registered against parcel 87/1 since 1974.

The entry refers, for its content, to the deed of grant no. 74-2213, concluded in settlement of a dispute about drainage and registered on 4 March 1974; its wording has not since been altered, and neither party asserts an agreement outside it. The clause on which both sides rely reads:

Registered in favour of the respective owner of parcel 87/3: a right of way for agricultural passage across the meadow track of parcel 87/1 to the fields on the creek side, to be exercised with consideration for the servient parcel; the upkeep of the track is borne by the entitled owner.

The plaintiff, who took parcel 87/1 by inheritance in 2003, submits that the right was granted for the passage then usual. Until 2006 the defendant's parents crossed six to ten times a year with a tractor and a small trailer, always after a word beforehand. Since the defendant took over the farm in 2007 and turned to asparagus and maize there have been some fifty crossings a year, unannounced, with a self-propelled harvester and trailers of up to eighteen tonnes. The verge is rutted and the ditch culvert is cracked.

He claimed an order limiting the exercise of the servitude to twelve crossings in each year, each announced on the previous day, and forbidding vehicles of more than eight tonnes; in the alternative, that the defendant keep to the made track and restore the culvert. The defendant answers that the deed sets no number and that his machines are those of ordinary farming in the district today. The Landgericht dismissed the action in its entirety. With his appeal the plaintiff pursues the claims of the first instance.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible. It is unfounded in so far as it seeks a limit on the number of crossings, a ban on the machinery used and an announcement before each crossing, and founded in so far as it concerns the route of the passage and the damaged culvert. That the servitude was created between the parties' predecessors is immaterial; it binds the plaintiff as the present owner of the servient parcel (Senate, judgment of 4 June 2013 – 4 U 23/13).
II. 1.

The content and the extent of a Grunddienstbarkeit follow from the entry in the register and from the deed to which the entry refers, construed under §§ 133, 157 BGB from the wording and from the purpose it discloses (§ 1018 BGB). The deed states that purpose: agricultural passage to the fields on the creek side. A servitude so granted does not hold the dominant parcel to the cultivation of the year of the grant. It covers the passage which the farming of that parcel requires as that farming develops, and a turn to crops needing heavier machines and more frequent journeys is such a development.

The limit lies in the kind of the use and not in its quantity. The servitude would be exceeded if the track served a parcel other than the dominant one, or an undertaking which is no longer agriculture, so that the burden changed in character, not in degree. Fifty crossings a year with the machinery now ordinary in the district show no such change. A right of way which secures the working of a farm would be worth little if it were held to the journeys of a horse cart.

§ 1020 sentence 1 BGB requires the entitled owner to exercise the servitude with the least possible interference. That duty governs the manner of the exercise: the route, the speed and the care owed to the installations of the servient owner, in particular a ditch and its culvert. It does not empower the court to fix a quota of journeys; a numerical cap would take from the servitude what the deed grants. That the deed puts the upkeep of the track on the entitled owner (§ 1021 BGB) confirms that the parties reckoned with wear from use. The subsidiary claim therefore succeeds: the defendant must keep to the made track and, having damaged the culvert in breach of that duty, make it good (§ 823 Abs. 1, § 249 Abs. 1 BGB).

An announcement before each crossing is owed only where the deed so provides. This deed does not; it requires consideration, not notice. The plaintiff relies on a note accompanying the settlement of 1974 and on the practice of the decades that followed, in which a word was in fact given each time. The note reads:
The passage will be taken up, as before, only after a word to the owner of 87/1, so that the cattle may be brought in from the meadow beforehand.

Neither the note nor the practice narrows the registered right. A courtesy which the entitled owner shows, here explained by a use of the meadow that ended long ago, is a revocable accommodation and not a term of the servitude; conversely, years of asking first create no right where none is registered (Landgericht Grevenau, judgment of 14 October 2014 – 7 O 150/13). A burden which every later acquirer must be able to read from the register and the deed cannot be cut down by conduct that neither records.

The decision on costs follows from § 92 Abs. 1 ZPO; the plaintiff prevails only on the subsidiary claim, whose weight the Senate puts at one fifth. Provisional enforceability follows from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The revision is not admitted, because the case turns on the construction of a single deed and raises no question of general importance (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO).

subject: A declaratory action about a strip of land: the interest exists when the neighbour disputes the line by conduct, the claim fails when the register and the survey agree
bears_on: case_orchard page 1 (the claimant seeks a declaration that the strip belongs to parcel 114/2) and page 2 (the registry geometry puts the strip in 114/3)
titelzeile: Declaratory action about a boundary strip: interest from the neighbour's conduct, register and survey decide the ownership
tenor: The action for a declaration that the strip of land between the fence and the registered boundary of parcels 52/4 and 52/5 of the Grevenau land registry forms part of parcel 52/4 is dismissed.
The plaintiff bears the costs of the proceedings, including the costs of the survey obtained by the chamber.
The judgment is provisionally enforceable against security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum to be enforced in each case.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff, a market gardener, is the registered owner of parcel 52/4 of the Grevenau land registry, on which he grows soft fruit under tunnels. The defendant, the arable farm of the family Vogtmann, is the registered owner of the adjoining parcel 52/5 to the east. A wire fence on chestnut posts, put up by the plaintiff's predecessor in 1984, runs the length of the common frontier. In dispute is a strip about 1.8 metres wide and 95 metres long lying immediately west of that fence, on which the plaintiff keeps a hose reel, a row of currant bushes and a compost heap, and over which he turns his machines.

From the autumn of 2014 the defendant mowed the strip twice, drove trailers along it and, in April 2015, ploughed its northern thirty metres into his field and sowed them. The plaintiff objected by letter of 20 April 2015; the defendant did not answer and carried on. The plaintiff contends that the fence has marked the boundary for more than thirty years and that his family alone has used the strip, which is therefore part of his parcel. He asks the chamber to declare that the strip belongs to parcel 52/4. The defendant asks that the action be dismissed. He has never said in words, he submits, that the boundary runs elsewhere, so that there is nothing between the parties which could be declared; in any event the register decides.

The chamber obtained a plan from the public surveyor W., who set the registered boundary between the two parcels out on the ground on 2 September 2016. The plan places that boundary 1.8 metres west of the fence along the whole of its length, so that the fence stands within parcel 52/5 as the register draws it and the disputed strip lies wholly in that parcel. The plaintiff has not contested the measurement. The chamber further heard the witness M., who has farmed the land to the north since 1990, on the use of the strip.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The action is admissible. Under § 256 Abs. 1 ZPO a declaration may be sought where the plaintiff has a legal interest in the immediate determination of a legal relationship; the ownership of a defined strip of land is such a relationship, and the interest exists where the defendant disputes the plaintiff's right. A boundary is disputed by conduct as well as by words. A neighbour who ploughs a strip into his field, sows it and drives his trailers along it as though it lay within his own parcel, and who does not desist when the owner objects in writing, asserts by those acts a right of his own to the land. That he has never put the assertion into words does not make the dispute less real, and the plaintiff need not wait for a letter.

Nor is the plaintiff confined to an action for the defendant's consent to a correction of the register under § 894 BGB. Such an action would turn on the same question, namely whether the strip belongs to the plaintiff's parcel, and would settle no more of what divides the parties in the field than the declaration settles. Where the action for performance offers no greater protection, the priority ordinarily accorded to it does not apply.
II.

The action is unfounded. The strip belongs to parcel 52/5. The land register describes each parcel by reference to the cadastral map, so that the defendant's ownership reaches as far as the map draws parcel 52/5, and the plan of the public surveyor W. sets that line out on the ground. The plan is a public document and proves the position of the recorded boundary until the contrary is shown (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, order of 22 March 2011 – 4 W 9/11); the plaintiff does not contest it. The fence tells against nothing: a boundary lies where the register and the survey put it, not where a fence has stood (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08). Under § 891 BGB the defendant, as the registered owner, is presumed to own the land within that line.

The presumption is not rebutted. It gives way only to proof that the register is inaccurate, that is, to proof of facts which would carry a claim for its correction under § 894 BGB; evidence of how the land has been used is not such proof. The witness M. confirmed that the fence has stood in its present line since at least 1990 and that the plaintiff and his predecessor alone tended the strip. The chamber accepts that account. It says nothing about where the boundary is recorded, still less that the record is wrong. Long use acquires no title, for prescription under § 900 BGB asks for thirty years of registration and not for thirty years of use (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 11 September 2012 – 4 U 140/11). The declaration sought must therefore be refused.
III.

The decision on costs follows from § 91 Abs. 1 ZPO and covers the costs of the survey, which the plaintiff's case made necessary. Provisional enforceability follows from § 709 Satz 1 ZPO. Whether the plaintiff may demand compensation for the bushes he has planted and tended on the defendant's land is not before the chamber and remains open (see the judgment of this chamber of 3 November 2010 – 2 O 311/09).

tatbestand.text: The parties are neighbouring landowners in the district of Grevenau. The plaintiff, the market gardener K., has owned parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry since 2007 and grows vegetables and soft fruit on it. The defendant, the farm of the family Mertens, works the adjoining parcel 87/2 to the east. Along the hawthorn hedge that divides the parcels there runs, on the western side, a strip of about 2.4 metres by 150 metres carrying a drainage ditch and a gravel track. The track leads north to a meadow of parcel 87/2 by the Greven creek, which a belt of alder and a wet hollow cut off from the defendant's farmyard. The defendant reaches that meadow over the track, since 2014 with increasing frequency.

The plaintiff sought a declaration that the strip forms part of parcel 87/1 and an order that the defendant cease driving over it. The defendant relied on an old field sketch placing the boundary west of the hedge and, in the alternative, on a way of necessity. The chamber obtained the plan of the public surveyor F. of 3 September 2015, which puts the registered line along the hedge, so that ditch and track lie within parcel 87/1. By the judgment under appeal it granted the declaration, holding that register and survey agree and that a private sketch does not contest a public document, and it dismissed the claim to cease driving, because the meadow could be reached only over the track (§ 917 BGB).

The plaintiff appeals against the dismissal of that claim; the declaration has become final. He contends that the meadow can be reached over the defendant's own land along the alder belt, so that no way of necessity arises. The defendant asks that the appeal be dismissed and has produced, with its reply of 14 November 2016, a certified extract of the folio of parcel 87/1 dated 9 November 2016. Section II records under no. 2, registered on 3 March 1987 upon a settlement between the parties' predecessors, a right of way for the respective owner of parcel 87/2 for passage with agricultural vehicles over the track along the hedge to the meadow. Neither party mentioned the entry at first instance.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in due form and time, and the value of the grievance exceeds the threshold of § 511 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 ZPO. It is unfounded. What remains in dispute is the claim to cease driving; the declaration binds the Senate, which proceeds on the footing that ditch and track lie within parcel 87/1. Under § 529 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 ZPO the Senate takes over the findings of the chamber, no concrete indication casting doubt on their completeness or correctness, and adds to them the certified extract of 9 November 2016, which falls to be considered for two independent reasons.
II.

The extract is admissible as a new means of defence under § 531 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 ZPO. Whether its late production rests on negligence is measured by what a party proceeding with ordinary care had reason to bring forward, and the defendant had no such reason. The case was fought over the course of the boundary and, failing that, over a way of necessity; the defendant drove the track as its predecessors had driven it; and the entry stands in the folio of the plaintiff's parcel, not in its own, a servitude needing no note on the folio of the benefited land. That the register is open to anyone with a legitimate interest does not make its content known to the parties.
III.

The entry would have to be considered even if the omission were negligent. What the extract shows is not in dispute; a certified extract proves the content of the register (§ 418 Abs. 1 ZPO), and the plaintiff disputes only its use. The preclusion of § 531 Abs. 2 ZPO spares the appellate court a taking of evidence that belonged below, and it has no object where nothing needs proving. Beyond that, a registered easement is not material a party may deploy or withhold, but a legal fact: § 891 Abs. 1 BGB presumes the registered right to exist, and the presumption operates from the moment the register lies before the court.
IV.

A court may therefore not set the register aside as coming too late. A judgment forbidding the defendant every crossing, while the register records its right to cross, would resolve nothing between the parties: the defendant would sue for toleration the next day, and two titles would stand against one another. The register's content is not a fact a court may ignore once it is before it. The Senate accordingly decides the case on the register as it stands, and it does so without remitting the matter, no further finding of fact being required (§ 538 Abs. 1 ZPO).
V.

The claim to cease driving is unfounded. The right of way was created by agreement and registration (§§ 873, 1018 BGB), binds the plaintiff as owner of the servient parcel and is untouched by the finding that the strip lies within his land (Senate, judgment of 4 June 2013 – 4 U 23/13). Its content follows from the entry and the deed to which it refers: passage to the meadow over the track along the hedge, which is the strip declared the plaintiff's. Passage with the tractors and trailers farming uses today serves that purpose (Senate, judgment of 17 May 2016 – 4 U 12/16).
VI.

The plaintiff has not sought to rebut the presumption of § 891 Abs. 1 BGB; that he did not know of the entry is no ground of rebuttal, for the register is wrong only where the registered right does not exist. Whether a way of necessity would also arise may remain open, a registered right of way leaving § 917 BGB no room (Senate, order of 28 January 2014 – 4 W 41/13). The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO. § 97 Abs. 2 ZPO does not displace it. That provision loads the costs on the successful party where it prevails on means it was in a position to advance at first instance, and the defendant was not in that position for the reasons given under II: the entry came to light only when the Grundbuchamt answered its enquiry about the drainage of the fields, and a party which has no occasion to suspect a servitude over the neighbour's parcel is not able, in the sense of § 97 Abs. 2, to produce its entry earlier. The costs of the certified extract therefore fall with the appeal. The decision on provisional enforceability follows from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. The revision is not admitted (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO).

subject: Knowing that a hall stands by a creek is not knowing of a defect: § 536b BGB and a gate that fails later
bears_on: case_mill page 1 (a five-year lease of the turbine hall of a historic water mill on the Greven creek) and page 3 (the gate reported jammed in September 2024, three years into the lease)
titelzeile: Rent reduction: a hall by the creek, § 536b BGB, and a flood gate that jams later
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 8 February 2017 – 7 O 84/16 – is dismissed.
The plaintiff bears the costs of the appeal proceedings.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 percent of the sum enforceable, unless the defendant first provides security in the same amount.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff lets commercial premises in the former dyeworks on the northern bank of the Greven creek. By a written lease of 4 March 2012 it let the ground-floor hall and the adjoining low store to the defendant, a joinery, for ten years at a monthly rent of 980 euros. The hall stands some twelve metres from the water. The low store is protected against high water by a flood gate set into the outer wall, which the plaintiff had installed in 2004 and which it has since maintained. The defendant viewed the premises twice before signing the lease.

From the spring of 2015 water entered the low store on seven occasions, each time after the creek had risen. The plaintiff's caretaker had reported the flood gate jammed in August 2014; the repair was entered in the maintenance budget for the following year and was not carried out. The defendant notified the ingress in writing on each occasion, reduced the rent by one fifth from May 2015 and had withheld 4,116 euros by January 2017. The plaintiff terminated the lease for arrears and claimed payment before the Landgericht Grevenau, extending its claim as further months fell due.

The plaintiff submitted that the defendant had known when signing that the hall lies directly on the creek and that the district is subject to high water, and that marks of earlier flooding were plainly visible on the wall of the store at the viewing. The defendant had therefore accepted the premises in the condition complained of and was barred by § 536b BGB from any reduction, at least for want of a reservation of its rights. The Landgericht dismissed the claim. The plaintiff pursues its claim for payment on appeal; the defendant defends the judgment under attack.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was filed and reasoned in due time and in the required form. In the matter it has no success. The Landgericht rightly held that the rent for the months in dispute was reduced by operation of law, that the sums withheld were accordingly not in arrears, and that the arrears on which the termination was founded therefore do not exist. The plaintiff attacks the judgment only on the bar under § 536b BGB; it does not contest the rate of reduction found by the Landgericht, which for the days of ingress and for the standing impairment of the store in the months between them at least reaches the sums withheld (Senate, judgment of 24 April 2012 – 8 U 99/11).
II.

The recurring ingress of water into the low store is a defect within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB. It removes the store from the use agreed by contract on every day on which water stands in it, and it does so because the flood gate has not closed since August 2014. Keeping that gate in working order is part of the duty the plaintiff owes under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB to maintain the premises in a condition fit for the contractual use. A gate reported jammed is a defect from the report onwards, and entering the repair in the next year's budget discharges nothing (Senate, judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14). Fault is not required (Senate, judgment of 24 April 2012 – 8 U 99/11).

§ 536b Satz 1 BGB does not bar the reduction. The provision denies the tenant the rights under §§ 536, 536a BGB only in respect of a defect of which he knows at the conclusion of the lease. What the defendant knew in March 2012 was the situation of the building: a hall on the bank of a watercourse in a district that sees high water. That is not a defect. A defect is the departure of the actual condition from the condition owed, and a hall by a creek whose gate closes is in the condition owed. The marks on the store wall showed that water had stood there in the past; they did not show that the gate then in place would fail to hold it.

Nor was a reservation of rights required. § 536b Satz 3 BGB applies where the tenant accepts premises knowing them to be defective, and it therefore presupposes a defect existing at acceptance. The defect here arose in August 2014, more than two years after the premises had been handed over without it; the defendant could not have known then what had not yet happened, so that § 536b Satz 2 BGB is likewise inapplicable. The rent was reduced by operation of law, and rent lawfully reduced is not rent in arrears (Senate, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09).
III.

The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO; the plaintiff bears the costs of an appeal that has failed in its entirety. The decision on provisional enforceability follows from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. There was no occasion to admit an appeal on points of law under § 543 Abs. 2 ZPO: the case turns on the application of settled principles to the condition of a single hall, and the Senate departs from none of its earlier decisions.

subject: Reaching the creek across a neighbour's land: riparian use gives no right of passage, an easement does, and what 'to the creek across the ditch track' covers
bears_on: case_orchard page 4 (the deed was granted in settlement of an earlier drainage dispute, for agricultural passage to the Greven creek across the ditch track) and page 1 (the irrigation ditch)
titelzeile: Reaching the creek across a neighbour's land: riparian freedom of use, registered easement, way of necessity
leitsatz: The freedom of use of a watercourse conferred by the state water act is a permission of public law addressed to those who can lawfully reach the water. It confers no private right to cross the land of another to get to the bank; such access is secured only by an easement under § 1018 BGB or, on the strict conditions of § 917 BGB, by a way of necessity.

An easement for passage to the creek across the ditch track covers reaching the watercourse in order to drain into it and to draw water from it within the limits of the water law, and with it the upkeep of the drainage ditch that leads there. Its scope follows the purpose recorded, not the technique of the year of grant.
tenor: On the appeal of the plaintiff the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 9 November 2017 – 2 O 88/17 – is amended as follows and the appeal is otherwise dismissed.

It is declared that under easement deed no. 94-2210 the plaintiff may use the ditch track on parcel 87/2 to reach the creek, so far as the water law permits, to drain into it, to draw water from it and to maintain the drainage ditch.
Of the costs of both instances the plaintiff bears two thirds and the defendant one third.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. Each party may avert enforcement by providing security of 110 per cent of the amount enforceable, unless the other party first provides security in the same amount.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff owns parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, on which he operates a market garden. The parcel does not adjoin the Greven creek. Between it and the creek lies parcel 87/2, arable land farmed by the defendant. A track along the eastern edge of parcel 87/2, known locally as the ditch track, runs from the plaintiff's field down to the bank; a drainage ditch runs beside it and discharges into the creek. Since 2015 the plaintiff has carried a pump to the bank in dry summers and has led the water of his field drains through that ditch into the creek.

In March 2017 the defendant closed the track with a steel barrier, ploughed the last thirty metres of the ditch flat and forbade the plaintiff the bank in writing. The plaintiff has applied principally for a declaration that he may reach and use the Greven creek at any point of the bank of parcel 87/2, free of the register, relying on the freedom of use of the creek that the state water act grants to everyone; that freedom, he submits, would be worthless if the riparian owner could shut off the way to the water. In the alternative he has applied for the same declaration confined to the ditch track, relying on easement deed no. 94-2210, registered on 4 February 1994 against parcel 87/2 for passage to the creek across that track.

The defendant has contended that the water act confers no right against him, that the easement was created for a herd long since given up and permits at most passage on foot, and that the clearing of the ditch and the laying of a pump line are not covered by it. The Landgericht dismissed the action. It held that the freedom of use is a matter of public law only, and that the easement, being silent as to the manner of its exercise, must be read narrowly. With his appeal the plaintiff pursues his declaratory applications; the defendant defends the judgment under attack.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible and succeeds to the extent set out in the operative part. The declaratory applications are admissible under § 256 ZPO. The defendant disputes the plaintiff's access by conduct, by a barrier and by a written prohibition, so that a present legal interest in the declaration exists; a declaration settles between the parties, for the future, what an order for the removal of the barrier alone would leave open.
II.

The principal application is unfounded. The freedom of use of surface waters conferred by the state water act allows anyone to bathe, to water livestock and to take water in the amounts the act allows; letting water into the creek, and abstraction beyond that measure, need the act's own permission. That freedom is a permission of public law: it says who may use the water, not over whose land the user may walk to reach it. It presupposes a person lawfully standing on the bank and creates no right in the neighbouring soil. The owner of the bank parcel accordingly remains entitled under § 903 BGB to exclude others, and the plaintiff can derive from the water act no right to cross parcel 87/2 at any point.

Access over the land of another is secured by private law alone: by a right of way registered as an easement under § 1018 BGB or, where a plot lacks the connection to a public road that its proper use requires, by a way of necessity under § 917 BGB. The strict conditions of § 917 BGB are not met here. The plaintiff's parcel is connected to the public field road to the north; what he lacks is not access to his land but access to the water, and a way of necessity is not granted to procure a particular convenience of cultivation. Nor is one needed where a registered right of way already provides the access (Fourth Civil Senate, decision of 28 January 2014 – 4 W 41/13).
III.

The application advanced in the alternative succeeds. Easement deed no. 94-2210 burdens parcel 87/2 in favour of the respective owner of parcel 87/1 and binds the defendant as the present owner (Fourth Civil Senate, judgment of 4 June 2013 – 4 U 23/13); that it was pleaded late and in the alternative does not matter: the register's content is not a fact a court may pass over (Fourth Civil Senate, judgment of 14 March 2017 – 4 U 118/16). Its recorded content, granted in settlement of an earlier dispute about drainage, is passage to the Greven creek across the ditch track. The purpose so recorded, and not the technique of the year of grant, determines the scope of the servitude (Fourth Civil Senate, judgment of 17 May 2016 – 4 U 12/16).

A passage granted to the creek is granted for that which one goes to the creek for. It therefore covers reaching the water in order to drain into it and to draw water from it, in each case only so far as the water law itself permits; the easement opens the way, it does not enlarge the permission. Because a right of way is worth nothing unless the way remains passable, it covers with it the upkeep of the drainage ditch that leads to the bank, its clearing included. Its exercise must remain considerate under § 1020 BGB: the plaintiff may bring a pump and the implements a holding of this size requires, but he may neither store anything on the track nor widen it.

The costs of both instances follow § 92 Abs. 1 ZPO. Measured against the two applications, the plaintiff has failed with the more valuable: access at any point of the bank, free of the register, is worth twice the corridor the register records, and the Senate accordingly puts two thirds of the total value on the application dismissed and one third on the declaration obtained. Provisional enforceability follows §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. There is no ground under § 543 Abs. 2 ZPO for leave to appeal on a point of law; the case turns on the construction of a single deed.

subject: Withholding rent to force a repair: how much a commercial tenant may retain beyond the reduction, and when the excess becomes default
bears_on: case_mill page 1 (Hartl withholds six months of rent, 8,400 euros, pleading a defect; the cooperative seeks termination)
titelzeile: Withholding rent to force a repair: the measure of retention beside the reduction, and the excess as default
leitsatz: Beside the reduction which operates by law under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB, a commercial tenant may retain part of the rent still owed under § 320 Abs. 1 BGB in order to press the landlord to remedy a notified defect. What is retained remains owed and falls due once the defect is remedied.

The measure of the retention is not at the tenant's discretion. It must be proportionate to the defect and to the pressure required, as a rule three to five times the monthly reduction, and never the whole rent for an unlimited time. What is withheld beyond that measure is in default and counts towards the threshold of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB.
tenor: The appeal of the defendant against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 3 May 2018 – 7 O 88/17 – is dismissed.
The defendant bears the costs of the appeal proceedings; the costs order of the first instance remains unaffected.

tatbestand.text: The parties are in dispute over the effect of a termination without notice for arrears of rent. By written lease of 9 September 2013 the plaintiff let to the defendant, which runs a bookbindery, a workshop hall with an adjoining paper store on parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, for a fixed term of ten years from 1 January 2014. The rent was agreed at 2,100 euros per month, payable in advance by the third working day of each month.

From the winter of 2015 rainwater ran down the inner face of the northern gable into the paper store whenever the rain was prolonged. The defendant kept a dated log with photographs and notified the plaintiff by letter of 14 March 2016; the plaintiff's caretaker countersigned four of the entries. The plaintiff obtained an estimate of 6,800 euros for the renewal of the roof flashing, entered that sum in the budget for the following year and did not have the works carried out.

By letter of 30 May 2016 the defendant announced that it would pay nothing further until the roof was repaired, and from 1 June 2016 it paid no rent at all. The plaintiff sent a reminder on 10 January 2017 and, by letter of 20 February 2017, declared termination without notice on account of arrears of 18,900 euros. The defendant vacated the hall in June 2017 under reservation of its rights; the roof was renewed in August 2017.

By judgment of 3 May 2018 the Landgericht Grevenau held the termination effective and ordered payment of the rent withheld, less a reduction of 20 per cent. The defendant appeals. It submits that a tenant faced with a defect which the landlord refuses to remedy may withhold the whole rent for as long as the defect lasts, so that no default can arise. The plaintiff defends the judgment and contends that a retention without limit is in truth a refusal to perform.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible. It was lodged in due form and within the time limit, the grounds were filed within the extended period, and the value of the subject matter of the appeal exceeds the threshold of § 511 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 ZPO. On the merits it has no success. The Landgericht rightly held that the lease was ended by the termination of 20 February 2017.
II.

The termination was effective under § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 lit. b BGB, because on the day it was declared the defendant was in default with an amount reaching two months' rent. Whether that threshold is reached is not answered by the sum the tenant kept back, but by so much of that sum as it was entitled to keep. Three amounts are to be distinguished: the rent not owed by reason of the reduction, the rent lawfully retained, and the excess.

The reduction operates by law and requires no declaration. Recurring ingress of rainwater into a store in which paper is kept is a defect within § 536 Abs. 1 BGB, and it is immaterial whether the landlord is at fault (Senate, judgment of 24 April 2012 – 8 U 99/11). The roof is a part of the building which the plaintiff owed in working condition, and the defect stood established from the notification of 14 March 2016 at the latest (Senate, judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14). Rent lawfully reduced is not rent in arrears (Senate, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09). The assessment of the reduction at 20 per cent, that is 420 euros a month, is not open to objection.

Beside the reduction the tenant may retain part of the rent still owed under § 320 Abs. 1 BGB in order to press the landlord to remedy the defect. The two remedies serve different ends: the reduction adjusts the price to the diminished enjoyment, the retention supplies the pressure which the tenant would otherwise have to obtain from a court. What is retained remains owed and falls due when the defect is remedied: the tenant who retains gains a delay, not a discount. Its measure, however, is not at the tenant's discretion. It must stand in a reasonable relation to the defect and to the pressure required, and it is bounded by § 242 BGB: as a rule three to five times the monthly reduction is permissible, the whole rent for an unlimited time is not.

The defendant's letter of 30 May 2016 is to be construed as a declaration of retention and not as a refusal to perform for good, for the defendant plainly wished to obtain the repair and not to keep the money. Measured against the standard set out above, however, what it announced went beyond the permissible measure. Its decisive passage reads:
Until the roof over the paper store is tight we shall transfer nothing. Every month you let pass without acting will cost you the full rent, and we intend to keep it that way for as long as it takes.

So read, the declaration claims the whole rent for an unlimited period and draws no distinction between the share not owed and the share retained. The defendant then acted upon it: it paid nothing for nine months, brought no action for the works, and offered the plaintiff no part of the sum it was holding, although the estimate for the repair had long been known to both sides.

The figures decide the case. Of the 18,900 euros withheld for the nine months from June 2016 to February 2017, 3,780 euros were not owed by reason of the reduction, and a further 2,100 euros, five times the monthly reduction, were lawfully retained. The remaining 13,020 euros were in default when the termination was declared and exceed two months' rent many times over. § 242 BGB does not assist the defendant, which never offered the retained sum. The decisions on costs and on provisional enforceability follow from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO and §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO.

norm: § 919 Abs. 1 BGB, § 919 Abs. 3 BGB, § 891 BGB
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 16. Februar 2018, Az: 2 O 25/18, Beschluss
subject: Setting the boundary marks after a survey: the duty to cooperate under § 919 BGB, and the fence is no defence
bears_on: case_orchard page 2 (the survey located the registered boundary; the fence stands 3.2 m west of it)
titelzeile: Setting boundary marks after a survey: the neighbour's duty to cooperate, and why an old fence is no defence
tenor: The immediate appeal of the appellant against the order of the Landgericht Grevenau of 15 November 2018 - 2 O 233/18 - is dismissed.
The appellant bears the costs of the appeal proceedings. The apportionment of the costs of the marking itself in equal shares, ordered by the chamber under § 919 Abs. 3 BGB, is unaffected.
The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is fixed at 3,200 euros, corresponding to the appellant's interest in resisting the marking of the surveyed line.

gruende.text: The respondent, a market gardener, is the owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry; the appellant owns the adjoining parcel 87/4 to the north. In April 2018 the respondent had the registered boundary located by a publicly appointed surveyor. The plan places the old post-and-wire fence between the two parcels 2.6 metres south of the registered line over its whole length of some 140 metres. Invited twice to attend a marking appointment, the appellant refused, stating that the fence had stood since 1974 and was the boundary. The chamber ordered him to cooperate in the setting of the boundary marks and apportioned the costs of the marking in equal shares.

The immediate appeal is admissible; it is directed against a decision the chamber was entitled to take by order, and it was lodged in time. It is, however, unfounded. Under § 919 Abs. 1 BGB every owner of a plot of land may demand of the owner of the adjoining plot that he cooperate in the setting of fixed boundary marks and, where existing marks have been displaced or have become unrecognisable, in their restoration. The claim follows from ownership alone; no further interest need be shown, and the refusal to attend an appointment properly offered is enough to found it. The manner of the marking and the procedure are governed by the provisions of the Land (§ 919 Abs. 2 BGB), which here require the attendance of both owners before the surveyor.

The marks are to be set on the registered boundary as located by the survey. In favour of the person registered as owner it is presumed that the right belongs to him (§ 891 BGB); the parcel to which that right attaches is the one the register describes by reference to the cadastre, and the course of its boundary is proved by the plan of a publicly appointed surveyor, a public document. It is met by proof that the register or the measurement is wrong, not by evidence of how the land has been used (Senate, order of 22 March 2011 - 4 W 9/11; Senate, judgment of 19 May 2009 - 4 U 62/08). Nothing of that kind has been offered here.

The objection that the old fence marks the boundary is no defence to the duty to cooperate. Marking is declaratory: it records where the boundary runs and neither creates, transfers nor extinguishes ownership, so that the appellant gives up nothing by attending. A fence standing 2.6 metres off the line is no boundary installation either (Senate, judgment of 21 April 2015 - 4 U 77/14), and years of use beyond it acquire no title (Senate, judgment of 11 September 2012 - 4 U 140/11). Whoever claims the strip between fence and line must pursue that claim in a title action; the marking leaves it open.

§ 920 BGB, on which the appellant relies in the alternative, is not opened. It applies only where the true course of the boundary cannot be ascertained; here it can be, from the register and from the survey. A boundary is not confused merely because one neighbour disputes it. The costs of the appeal proceedings follow from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO. The apportionment of the costs of the marking in equal shares corresponds to § 919 Abs. 3 BGB, no legal relationship between the parties providing otherwise. The value of the appeal proceedings has been fixed according to the appellant's interest in resisting the marking.

norm: § 543 Abs. 3 Satz 2 Nr. 3 BGB, § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB, § 536 BGB, § 522 Abs. 2 ZPO
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 18. Mai 2018, Az: 7 O 62/18, Beschluss
subject: No warning is needed before a commercial lease is terminated for arrears, but the notice must let the tenant check the figure
bears_on: case_mill page 1 (the cooperative claims six months of arrears and seeks termination; the tenant admits withholding and pleads a defect)
titelzeile: Termination of a commercial lease for arrears: no warning, but the figure named must let the tenant check it
tenor: The appeal of the defendant against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 8 November 2018 – 7 O 84/18 – is dismissed by unanimous order under § 522 Abs. 2 Satz 1 ZPO.
The defendant bears the costs of the appeal proceedings. The judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau referred to above is provisionally enforceable without provision of security.
The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set at 37,720 euros, of which 27,600 euros fall on the claim for surrender of the premises and 10,120 euros on the claim for payment.

gruende.text: The plaintiff lets the front hall of the old brewery yard in Grevenau to commercial tenants. The defendant, who runs a printing works, has held the hall since 2014 at a rent of 2,300 euros per month. The defendant paid nothing from January 2018 onwards. By letter of 14 June 2018, received the following day, the plaintiff terminated the lease without notice for arrears, naming an amount of 11,500 euros, and demanded the surrender of the hall. By judgment of 8 November 2018 the Landgericht ordered the defendant to vacate and surrender the hall and to pay 10,120 euros with interest.

With its appeal the defendant argues that the termination is invalid on two grounds. No warning preceded it, although the plaintiff had accepted late payment for years and the defendant could expect to be told before the lease was ended. And the figure named in the notice is wrong: it counts the rent for February to May 2018 in full, although the rent for those months stood reduced because damp from a defective roof made a third of the hall unusable. By order of 8 April 2019 the Senate gave notice of its intention to dismiss the appeal under § 522 Abs. 2 ZPO. The reply of 30 April 2019 gives no cause for a different assessment.

A warning was not required. Where the lease is terminated without notice because the tenant is in default with the rent, § 543 Abs. 3 Satz 2 Nr. 3 BGB dispenses both with the period for remedy and with the warning that § 543 Abs. 3 Satz 1 BGB otherwise demands. The statute has weighed that question itself, and the courts may not restore through good faith what the legislature has removed. Nor does the plaintiff's earlier indulgence create a duty to warn. Accepting a late payment is a forbearance about the past; it is not a promise about the future, and a tenant who pays nothing for five months cannot draw from it that the lease will be left standing.

The notice did not have to state its reasons either. The duty to give reasons in the declaration is confined by § 569 Abs. 4 BGB to residential leases and is not extended to commercial premises by § 578 BGB. It does not follow that a landlord who names a figure may name any figure at all. Where the notice states an amount of arrears, the tenant must be able to check it, that is, to relate it to identifiable months and to identifiable sums, whether from the notice itself or from the rent account and the reminders that preceded it. A round sum standing behind no month leaves the tenant unable to see what is demanded and to pay it off, and is no proper foundation for a termination.

The overstatement the defendant complains of does not defeat this notice. Rent lawfully reduced under § 536 BGB is not owed and therefore cannot fall into arrears; the reduction operates by law and requires no declaration (Senate, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09), so that a landlord who counts the reduced part into the figure names too high an amount. But the figure is not a condition of the termination. The condition is the default described in § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB. Where the arrears truly owed reach the threshold on their own, an inflated figure misstates the extent of the default and not its existence, and the notice stands. The Senate examines the true arrears itself.

On the defendant's own case the rent was reduced from February to May 2018 by fifteen per cent, that is by 345 euros in each of four months, together 1,380 euros. Deducted from the 11,500 euros named, 10,120 euros remained truly in arrears on 15 June 2018, more than four monthly rents and far beyond the two that § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB requires; what was withheld above the reduction was in default (Senate, judgment of 11 December 2018 – 8 U 88/18). The months and sums behind the figure appear from the rent account sent with the reminder of 22 May 2018, so the defendant could check the amount.

The appeal therefore manifestly has no prospect of success. The matter has no fundamental significance, neither the development of the law nor the consistency of case law requires a decision by judgment, and an oral hearing is not called for, the questions of law being settled and the figures undisputed. The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO. The judgment of the Landgericht is provisionally enforceable under §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 and 713 ZPO. The value in dispute is set at one year's rent for the claim for surrender and at the sum awarded for the claim for payment.
