subject: Twenty-five years of tolerated, announced crossings do not forfeit the owner's right against crossings of a different kind
bears_on: case_orchard page 3 (Tomas Rehn: crossings 'a few times a year, always with a word to the Albas first' until around 2018, after which frequent and unannounced)
titelzeile: Forfeiture and neighbourly toleration: announced occasional crossings do not cover frequent unannounced ones
tenor: On the appeal of the plaintiff the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 6 December 2018 – 2 O 187/18 – is amended: the defendant is ordered to refrain from crossing the plaintiff's parcel 87/1 with agricultural machinery without announcing the crossing beforehand.
For each case of contravention the defendant is threatened with an administrative fine of up to 250,000 euros or, in the alternative, with administrative detention of up to six months.
The defendant shall bear the costs of the proceedings at first instance and of the appeal.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. The defendant may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum enforceable, unless the plaintiff first provides security in the same amount.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff is the owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, a strip of meadow along whose southern edge an unmetalled farm track runs from the village road towards the fields. The defendant, a farming partnership, works parcel 87/6, which adjoins the plaintiff's land to the east and which can otherwise be reached only by an appreciably longer detour over the creek road. No right of way in favour of parcel 87/6 is entered in the land register against parcel 87/1, and none was ever granted in writing.

From 1992 onwards the defendant and its predecessor crossed the track with a tractor and trailer some four to six times a year, at the hay harvest and when the ditch was cleared. On each occasion someone from the farm asked the plaintiff beforehand, mostly by telephone, and the plaintiff agreed. In the spring of 2017 the defendant took a further eleven hectares behind the parcel into cultivation and acquired a self-propelled harvester weighing eighteen tonnes. Since then it crosses two to three times a week during the season, at any hour and without asking. The bank of the plaintiff's ditch has been pressed down over a length of some forty metres.

The plaintiff first demanded that the crossings cease in June 2017 and, when the defendant refused, brought the present action in the following spring. He states that he does not object to occasional crossings announced beforehand. The defendant submitted that after twenty-five years of undisturbed passage the plaintiff could no longer object, and that it had acquired the harvester in reliance on that practice. The Landgericht heard the farmer Domeier as a witness and dismissed the action, holding the claim forfeited under § 242 BGB. The plaintiff appeals and pursues his claim in the form now tenored; the defendant defends the judgment under appeal.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible. It was filed and reasoned in due time and in the proper form (§§ 511, 517, 519, 520 ZPO). The limitation of the claim to unannounced crossings, made in the statement of grounds of appeal, is a restriction of the application within the meaning of § 264 Nr. 2 ZPO and requires no consent; it takes from the claim only what the plaintiff never wished to have decided in his favour, namely the occasional announced passage which he continues to tolerate.
II.

The appeal is also well founded. The plaintiff may require the defendant to refrain from crossing parcel 87/1 without prior announcement (§ 1004 Abs. 1 Satz 2, § 903 BGB). Each crossing is an interference with the plaintiff's ownership, and the plaintiff is not obliged to tolerate it (§ 1004 Abs. 2 BGB). No easement is registered, and an agreed right of way would arise only upon entry in the land register (§ 873 BGB). A way of necessity does not arise either: § 917 Abs. 1 BGB requires that the plot lack the connection needed for its proper use, and a longer detour over the creek road is not such a lack. What the defendant had was a licence revocable at any time, as the Landgericht Grevenau has rightly held for a comparable practice (judgment of 14 October 2014 – 7 O 150/13).

The claim is not forfeited. Forfeiture under § 242 BGB requires two elements: a lapse of time, and circumstances from which the obligor could reasonably conclude that the obligee would no longer assert his right and in reliance on which the obligor has arranged his affairs. Time alone does not suffice, however long it runs; twenty-five years of toleration are not a period of prescription. The Senate has held for the neighbouring institute of acquisitive prescription that use, however long continued, creates no right (judgment of 11 September 2012 – 4 U 140/11); toleration can achieve no more.

The second element is lacking. What the plaintiff tolerated was a use of a particular kind, and the character of that use emerges from the evidence taken below, which the Senate adopts without repeating it (§ 529 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 ZPO). The witness Domeier, who farmed the land west of the track until 2015 and who has no interest in the outcome, described the earlier practice in these terms:

Four, five, six times in the year the tractor went over, in the hay and again in October. They always came up to the house first, or telephoned the evening before; and if it did not suit, they took the creek road and said nothing further about it.

The Senate finds this account credible, and the defendant has not contradicted it in substance. It describes a practice whose defining feature was the asking, and whose extent the plaintiff kept in his own hands from one occasion to the next. A use that depended upon being permitted each time cannot found the confidence that permission would never again be refused.

The crossings now complained of are not that use continued but a use of a different kind. Two or three passages a week are not four to six in the year; a harvester of eighteen tonnes is not a tractor with a trailer; and a crossing announced beforehand leaves the owner the decision which an unannounced crossing takes from him. Toleration is measured by what was tolerated. The Senate has held, for the scope of a registered right of way, that considerate exercise limits the manner and not the frequency of the use (judgment of 17 May 2016 – 4 U 12/16); that reasoning presupposes a right, and where no right exists it cannot be borrowed to enlarge a bare toleration.

It follows that the plaintiff may object to the new use without thereby objecting to the old, and that his continuing tolerance of announced crossings does not weaken his claim against unannounced ones. The risk of repetition is made out by the interferences that have occurred and has not been removed, the defendant having refused to give an undertaking. The order is limited accordingly. Costs follow § 91 Abs. 1 ZPO; the restriction of the claim on appeal caused no separate costs and is disregarded under § 92 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 ZPO. Provisional enforceability follows §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. Leave to appeal on a point of law is not granted, the requirements of § 543 Abs. 2 ZPO not being met.

norm: § 891 Abs. 1 BGB, § 894 BGB, § 286 ZPO
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 28. Juni 2019, Az: 2 O 136/19, Beschluss
subject: The register's presumption is rebutted by proof that the register is wrong, not by witnesses to how the land was used
bears_on: case_orchard page 3 (the witness statement on the fence and the use since 1991) against page 2 (the survey)
titelzeile: Rebutting the register's presumption: proof that the register is wrong, not witnesses to decades of use
tenor: The immediate complaint of the appellant against the order of the Landgericht Grevenau of 28 June 2019 – 2 O 136/19 –, by which the chamber refused to hear four further witnesses, is dismissed.
The appellant bears the costs of the complaint proceedings, including the costs necessarily incurred by the respondent in resisting the complaint.

The value in dispute for the complaint proceedings is set at 4,200 euros. The complaint on a point of law against this order is allowed, the question of what rebuts the register's presumption being of general significance.

gruende.text: The appellant is registered as owner of parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry; the respondent is registered as owner of the adjoining parcel 88 to the east. Before the chamber the appellant seeks a declaration that a strip some 2.6 metres wide and 210 metres long, lying east of an old hornbeam hedge, forms part of parcel 87/1, and an order that the respondent cease cutting it. A plan drawn up in 2018 by a publicly appointed surveyor places the registered boundary along the western foot of the hedge, so that on the register's geometry the strip lies within parcel 88.

The appellant does not attack the measurement. He offered four witnesses, among them the farmer of the parcel to the north, for the assertions that the hedge has stood in its present line since 1976, that he and his father alone mowed the strip, laid a drainage pipe beneath it and took its fruit, and that the respondent's predecessor entered it only after asking. By the order under complaint the chamber refused to hear those witnesses, holding what they were to say irrelevant. The immediate complaint against that refusal is admissible; it is unfounded.

In favour of the person registered in the land register as owner it is presumed that the right belongs to him (§ 891 Abs. 1 BGB). The presumption attaches to the parcel as the register describes it, and the register describes it through the cadastral records; it therefore covers the course of the registered boundary, which the plan of a publicly appointed surveyor proves as a public document (Senate, order of 22 March 2011 – 4 W 9/11). The presumption says nothing about how the ground has been worked, and it is not weakened by showing that the ground was worked otherwise.

It is rebutted only by the full proof, to the standard of § 286 ZPO, that the content of the register is incorrect, that is by proof of the facts which would carry a claim for correction under § 894 BGB: that the entry rests on a transfer which failed, that a parcel was divided otherwise than the cadastre records, or that the boundary was carried into the survey wrongly. Whoever would displace the register must therefore say what in it is false, and must offer his evidence upon that.

Evidence of use cannot do this. Mowing, planting, fencing, drainage and passage are exercises of possession, and possession is not title; the register speaks to who owns, not to who works. A witness who reports that a hedge or a fence has stood in one line for decades, and that one neighbour alone tended the ground beyond it, says nothing that could make the registered boundary false, however truthful and however long his memory. The Senate has held as much before (judgment of 19 May 2009 – 4 U 62/08; judgment of 11 September 2012 – 4 U 140/11): use of that length acquires no title either.

An offer of evidence upon a fact that could not alter the decision even if it were proved is irrelevant, and the court must refuse it; hearing it would not serve the finding of the truth (§ 286 ZPO) but would only delay the proceedings. The chamber was therefore right. Relevant would be an offer aimed at the incorrectness itself, or at a course that can no longer be ascertained, so that § 920 BGB would decide it; the appellant remains free to make one, and to plead a servitude or an agreement, which this order leaves untouched. The costs follow from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO; the complaint on a point of law is allowed, the question arising repeatedly in the district.

rechtsmittelbelehrung: Against this order a complaint on a point of law lies within one month of service, the Senate having allowed it; it must be lodged in writing, must designate the order challenged and must be signed by a lawyer admitted before the court which decides it.

norm: § 536 Abs. 1 BGB, § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB, § 286 ZPO
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 11. Oktober 2019, Az: 7 O 173/19, Urteil
subject: High water is a natural event, but water that a working flood gate would have kept out is the landlord's sphere: the defect is the gate, not the creek
bears_on: case_mill page 2 (nine ingress dates, each within two days of the creek's gauge exceeding 1.8 metres) and page 3 (the jammed flood gate)
titelzeile: Rent reduction for flooding: high water is a natural event, the failed flood gate is the landlord's defect
leitsatz: High water in a natural watercourse is an event outside the control of the parties and does not of itself make leased premises beside that watercourse defective within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB. Where the premises are equipped with an installation whose purpose is to keep that water out, its working condition belongs to the condition owed under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB.

If water enters because that installation has failed, the ingress lies in the landlord's sphere of risk; the defect is the failed installation, not the high water. That a working installation would have kept the water out may be found under § 286 ZPO from the coincidence of the dates of ingress with the exceeding of a stated gauge level.
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 4 February 2020 – 7 O 88/19 – is dismissed.
The costs of the appeal proceedings are borne by the plaintiff, including the costs occasioned by the taking of evidence before the Senate.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum enforceable, unless the defendant first provides security in the same amount.
The revision is not admitted; the questions raised are settled in the case law of this court and the case has no significance beyond itself.

tatbestand.text: By a written lease of 12 March 2015 the plaintiff let to the defendant, a joinery, a workshop hall with an adjoining basement store in the former grain store on parcel 87/1 of the Grevenau land registry, which stands on the eastern bank of the Greven creek. The term was ten years from 1 April 2015, the rent 2,100 euros a month. The store is reached by a loading ramp which is closed against the creek by a flood gate installed in 1998. The plaintiff claims 7,560 euros, being sums the defendant retained from the rent over twelve months from June 2018.

The defendant pleads a defect. Its log, kept with photographs, records water standing in the store on seven dates between November 2017 and March 2019, to a depth of up to twenty-two centimetres; a consignment of veneer and a pallet of adhesive were written off. The defendant reduced the rent for the months concerned by thirty per cent. It relies on an inspection report of the plaintiff's caretaker of 12 October 2017, which records the gate's lower seal as perished and its runner as corroded, on the plaintiff's maintenance budget for 2018, in which the repair of the gate appears, and on the fact that the gate was not repaired until August 2019.

The Landgericht heard the caretaker, obtained the readings of the creek gauge from the water authority and dismissed the claim. It held that the rent was reduced by operation of law and that the retained sums were never owed. With its appeal the plaintiff pursues the claim further. It submits that the flooding of the Greven creek is a natural event beyond anyone's control, which struck the whole lower valley in those winters; that premises on a creek are not defective merely because the creek rises; and that the defendant took the store knowing where it stands. The defendant defends the judgment under attack.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible; it was lodged and reasoned in due form and within the time allowed. It is unfounded. The chamber rightly held that the rent for the months in dispute was reduced by operation of law under § 536 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB, so that the sums retained were not owed and the plaintiff's claim for their payment is without foundation.
II.

Leased premises are defective within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB where their actual condition departs, to the disadvantage of the tenant, from the condition owed; what is owed follows in the first place from § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB, under which the landlord must maintain the premises in a condition fit for the contractual use throughout the term. To this extent the Senate follows the appeal: a natural event which no party controls, such as the rising of a watercourse after rain, does not of itself make premises beside that watercourse defective. The landlord does not owe a creek that stays low.

That, however, is not this case. Where the premises are equipped with an installation whose very purpose is to keep that water out, the working condition of the installation belongs to the condition owed, and the landlord must preserve it for the term. Water which passes a gate that no longer closes does not enter as a natural event; it enters through the gap the landlord has left open. The defect is the gate, not the creek, and the ingress lies in the landlord's sphere of risk. The 8th Civil Senate of this court has so held for a gate reported as jammed, adding that budgeting the repair for the following year is no discharge (judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14); fault is not required (judgment of 24 April 2012 – 8 U 99/11).

The Senate is satisfied, to the degree of certainty required by § 286 ZPO, that a working gate would have kept the water out. The seven dates in the defendant's log each fall on, or within one day of, a day on which the gauge at the Grevenau road bridge exceeded 2.10 metres; on no day on which the gauge remained below that mark did water enter the store, although the store was in daily use throughout. That coincidence, taken with the caretaker's report of the perished seal and with the expert's finding that a gate closing flush holds a head of water of some sixty centimetres, leaves no doubt useful in practical life. Certainty does not require the exclusion of every conceivable possibility.

The remaining objections of the plaintiff do not carry. That the defendant knew the store stands beside the creek is not knowledge of a defect within § 536b BGB; it took premises whose gate then worked, and a gate which fails later is a defect arising during the term (8th Civil Senate, judgment of 19 September 2017 – 8 U 52/17). Nor may a landlord who has recognised the repair as necessary, budgeted for it and then deferred it describe the consequences of its own omission as force majeure. The measure of the reduction found by the chamber is not attacked in its amount and is not open to objection.
III.

The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, that on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. There was no ground to admit the revision under § 543 Abs. 2 ZPO; the case turns on the application of settled principles to the condition of a single gate.

norm: § 242 BGB, § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB, § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB, § 286 ZPO
vorinstanz: vorgehend LG Grevenau, 22. Mai 2020, Az: 7 O 210/20, Urteil
subject: A landlord who defers a budgeted repair to press the tenant out cannot terminate for the arrears it thereby caused
bears_on: case_mill page 3 (an internal note of February 2025: 'defer gate works until the lease question with H. is resolved'; the repair budgeted for 2025 and not done)
titelzeile: Termination for arrears after a repair deliberately deferred: the landlord may not rely on a default it caused
leitsatz: A landlord who withholds a repair it owes under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB in order to bring the tenant into default and obtain a ground of termination acts contrary to good faith, § 242 BGB. Arrears accumulating while the notified defect is left unremedied for that reason cannot found a termination under § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB.

An internal note of the landlord recording that the works are to be held back until the question of the tenancy is settled is an admission of the party which the court may make the basis of its conviction under § 286 ZPO. Reasons for the delay asserted only in the proceedings do not displace it.
tenor: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 3 September 2020 – 7 O 121/19 – is dismissed.
The plaintiff bears the costs of the appeal proceedings; the costs order of the first instance remains unaffected by this judgment.

The judgment is provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by providing security in the amount of 110 per cent of the sum enforceable, unless the defendant first provides security in the same proportion.

tatbestand.text: The parties are in dispute about the continuation of a commercial lease. By written contract of 2 April 2014 the plaintiff, a property company which owns the former granary on the eastern bank of the Greven creek, let the workshop wing of that building to the defendant, a joinery, for a fixed term of ten years at a monthly rent of 1,850 euros. The wing includes a machine store on the ground floor, into which the surface water of the yard is led through a channel and a drain grate. The plaintiff claims possession and the arrears.

In May 2016 the plaintiff's own property manager reported the yard drain as jammed. The repair was entered in the maintenance plan for 2017 at 6,400 euros and was not carried out. Between August 2016 and November 2018 water stood in the machine store on eight occasions after prolonged rain; the property manager countersigned four of the entries in the defendant's dated log. The defendant notified each event and demanded the repair by letters of 12 September 2016 and 4 April 2017. From September 2017 it withheld half of the monthly rent.

The plaintiff's file contains an internal note of 8 March 2017 concerning the drain works, which it produced in the first instance on the order of the Landgericht. By letter of 14 January 2019 the plaintiff terminated the lease without notice on account of arrears which it put at 14,800 euros, and brought the present action for possession and for payment of the arrears of 14,800 euros. It has contended that the works were postponed only because no contractor could be had at an acceptable price, and that a tenant withholding half the rent for years is in default whatever the landlord's conduct.

The Landgericht dismissed the action for possession and ordered the defendant to pay 4,300 euros of the withheld rent. It held that the rent was reduced for the months in which the store could not be used, and that the plaintiff was barred from relying on the remaining arrears because it had itself held back the remedy. With its appeal the plaintiff pursues the claim for possession alone. The defendant defends the judgment under appeal and relies in particular on the internal note.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible. It was lodged in due form and within the time limit, the grounds were filed in time, and the value of the subject matter of the appeal exceeds the threshold of § 511 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 ZPO. On the merits it has no success. The lease was not brought to an end by the declaration of 14 January 2019, so that the plaintiff has no claim to possession under § 546 Abs. 1 BGB.
II.

A termination without notice under § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB requires that the tenant be in default with the rent in the amount there described. Rent which is reduced by operation of law because of a defect is not owed and is not rent in arrears (Senate, judgment of 6 October 2009 – 8 U 30/09). Beside the reduction the tenant may retain a further part of the rent to press for the remedy; what it withholds above that measure is in default (Senate, judgment of 11 December 2018 – 8 U 88/18).

The machine store was defective. Under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB the plaintiff owes the premises in a condition fit for the contractual use, and that duty covers the drainage that keeps the yard water out. An installation reported as jammed by the landlord's own manager is defective from the day of the report, and entering the repair in the plan for the following year discharges nothing (Senate, judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14). On the findings of the Landgericht the rent was reduced for the months affected; to that extent nothing fell into arrears. The retention went beyond the reduction, so that a part of the sum claimed was owed and unpaid.

That remainder the plaintiff may not rely on. The internal note of 8 March 2017 is an admission of a party which the court may make the basis of its conviction under § 286 ZPO. It was not written for the proceedings and states no position; it records what the plaintiff decided at the time, and the plaintiff has not disputed its authenticity. It reads:

Drain and yard channel: hold the works back for now. Nothing is to be commissioned until the matter of the tenancy in the workshop wing is settled. The sum stays in the plan; release only once that question is decided.

The note admits of no other reading. It weighs neither the cost of the works, nor the season, nor the availability of a contractor. It makes the repair, and the release of a sum already budgeted, depend on the outcome of the dispute with the tenant.

A landlord who deliberately withholds a repair it owes in order to bring the tenant into default and so to obtain a ground of termination acts contrary to good faith, § 242 BGB. The default is then its own work. Arrears which accumulate while the landlord holds back the remedy of a notified defect cannot found a termination under § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB, because the ground relied on has been produced by the party which invokes it. Whether the tenant measured its retention correctly need not be decided; the excess arose in the same period and from the same cause.

The objections of the plaintiff do not carry. That no contractor could be found is contradicted by its own note, which makes the works turn on the tenancy and not the market; no enquiry and no refusal are named. That no warning was required before the termination (Senate, decision of 14 May 2019 – 8 W 21/19) is correct but beside the point: what is objected to is not the form of the notice but the ground. Reasons for the delay first asserted in the proceedings cannot displace the plaintiff's own record of its decision.

The termination of 14 January 2019 was therefore ineffective and the lease continued, so that the claim for possession is unfounded and the appeal is dismissed. The decision on costs follows from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, that on provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO. There was no occasion to allow an appeal on points of law; the Senate applies settled principles to the facts of this case.

tatbestand.text: The parties are in dispute about the continuation of a commercial lease. By written contract of 1 March 2019 the plaintiff let to the defendant, a dairy which ripens and sells cheese in small lots, the vaulted cellar and the loading floor of the former brewery on parcel 63/4 of the Grevenau land registry for a fixed term of five years at a rent of 1,100 euros a month, payable in advance by the third day of each month. The cellar is drained through a yard gully at the foot of the loading ramp. The plaintiff claims possession of the premises and payment of 3,300 euros.

On 6 July 2021 the plaintiff's caretaker recorded in the maintenance file that the gully was silted and would no longer take the yard water; the defendant sent the plaintiff a copy of that note on the following day. The repair was carried into the maintenance budget for the following year and was not executed. After heavy rain water ran down the ramp into the cellar on 14 September and again on 12 November 2021. A batch of ripening cheese invoiced at 1,860 euros was spoiled on the first occasion and a delivery invoiced at 940 euros on the second; both were destroyed.

The defendant paid no rent for October, November and December 2021. By letter of 20 December 2021 it declared that it set off its claim to damages, 2,800 euros in all, against those rents. By letter of 7 January 2022, received on 10 January 2022, the plaintiff terminated the lease without notice on account of arrears which it itemised at 3,300 euros. It submits that a claim to damages which is disputed and not liquidated cannot be set off against rent, and that the defendant ought to have paid and sued for its loss separately. The defendant relies on the set-off and on its retroactive effect.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The action is admissible, but for the greater part unfounded. A termination without notice under § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB requires that the arrears be in existence at the moment the notice reaches the tenant, and what is then owed follows from the state of the account as the law leaves it at that moment; a set-off already declared belongs to that state of the account, and if what remains after it still reaches the threshold, the notice stands and the set-off has reduced the debt alone. In form the notice was unobjectionable: it set out the three rents and so allowed the defendant to check the figure (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, order of 14 May 2019 – 8 W 21/19).
II.

The defendant held a claim to damages of 2,800 euros under § 536a Abs. 1 BGB. A yard gully which no longer takes the water is a defect of the premises from the day it is reported, and carrying the work into the next year's budget is no discharge but the deferral itself (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14); water which a working drain would have held out lies in the landlord's sphere, not in the weather (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 27 October 2020 – 12 U 19/20). No share of the loss falls on the defendant under § 254 Abs. 1 BGB: after the first ingress it raised its stock onto racks, and the second batch was spoiled on the day it arrived (this chamber, judgment of 23 February 2016 – 7 O 199/15).

The set-off was effective. Both parties owed money of the same kind, the rents were due, and the counterclaim was due and enforceable, so that § 387 BGB is satisfied. That the plaintiff disputes the counterclaim is immaterial: a claim need not be admitted or liquidated to be set off, it need only be well founded, and the chamber has found it so. What the law does require is the declaration prescribed by § 388 BGB. A tenant who merely retains the rent, however good its reason, has not set off (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 11 December 2018 – 8 U 88/18); it is then thrown back on § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 3 BGB, which saves the lease only if the declaration follows immediately upon the notice. Here it preceded the notice by eighteen days.

Under § 389 BGB the set-off extinguishes the claims, so far as they cover each other, from the moment at which they first stood against each other fit for set-off; no allocation having been made, the counterclaim falls on the oldest debt (§ 396 Abs. 1 Satz 2, § 366 Abs. 2 BGB). The 1,860 euros accordingly wiped out the rent for October and 760 euros of that for November, and the 940 euros, which arose on 12 November 2021, the remaining 340 euros of November and 600 euros of December. When the notice arrived, 500 euros stood open, from a single due date. That is neither default at two consecutive dates with the rent or a not insignificant part of it, nor arrears reaching two months' rent, here 2,200 euros; both alternatives of the provision therefore fail.
III.

Whether the rent was in addition reduced under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB for the days of ingress, and whether the plaintiff would be barred in any event by its deferral of a budgeted repair (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 15 June 2021 – 8 U 3/21), may be left open, the threshold not being reached even on the full rent. The claim to payment succeeds in the sum of 500 euros, with interest from 4 December 2021, that rent having fallen due on the third day of the month without any reminder being needed (§ 286 Abs. 2 Nr. 1, § 288 Abs. 2 BGB). The decision on costs rests on § 92 Abs. 1 ZPO, that on provisional enforceability on § 709 Satz 1 and 2 ZPO.

subject: The owner of a historic water mill holds the old water right and the duty that comes with it: the mill race and its flood protection are the owner's, not the tenant's
bears_on: case_mill page 1 (the Greven Mill Cooperative owns the historic water mill on the Greven creek and lets its turbine hall) and page 3 (the flood gate)
titelzeile: Historic water mill: the old water right, the mill race and the flood protection are the owner's duty
leitsatz: The old water right attached to a historic water mill entitles the owner to divert the creek into the mill race and to use its flow for the mill, and obliges the owner, as the counterpart of that entitlement, to keep the race, its walls, its head and tail gates and the flood protection of the mill buildings in working order.

That duty rests on the owner under public water law and, toward the tenant of part of the mill buildings, under § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB. It is not shifted to the tenant by the mere circumstance that the object let is a hall in a mill on a creek. A gate that fails is the landlord's defect under § 536 Abs. 1 BGB.

This judgment and the judgment of the Landgericht are provisionally enforceable. The plaintiff may avert enforcement by providing security of 110 per cent of the enforceable sum, unless the defendant first provides security in the same amount.
The appeal on points of law is not admitted. The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is set at 31,160 euros.

tatbestand.text: The plaintiff is the owner of a historic water mill on the Greven creek at Sanden, entered on parcel 63/4 of the Grevenau land registry, together with the mill race that branches from the creek some 180 metres above the mill house and returns to it below. Since 2016 the plaintiff has let the mill's machine hall, some 240 square metres, to the defendant, a joinery, at 1,900 euros a month. The storage part of the hall adjoins the wall of the race. The plaintiff claims 11,400 euros of withheld rent for the twelve months from March 2021 and possession of the hall.

The defendant has retained half the rent since March 2021 and pleads a defect. Its dated log, kept with photographs, records water entering the hall on seven occasions between November 2020 and January 2022; on each occasion the gauge of the creek at Sanden had exceeded 1.7 metres within the preceding two days. The head gate of the race, by which the flow can be shut off above the mill, was reported to the plaintiff as jammed in August 2020 by the miller in the plaintiff's employ, and the wall of the race below it was silted to within twenty centimetres of its crest. Nothing was done before the action; the plaintiff had the gate freed at the end of January 2022, after service.

The Landgericht ordered the defendant to pay 3,040 euros with interest and dismissed the claim for the remainder, in particular the claim for possession. It held that the hall had been defective from the report of the jammed gate, assessed the reduction at 40 per cent for the eleven months during which the gate remained jammed and the storage part lay open to the race, and found the arrears remaining after that reduction below the threshold of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 BGB. The plaintiff pursues the rest of its claim on appeal; the defendant defends the judgment.

entscheidungsgruende.text: I.

The appeal is admissible but unfounded. The Landgericht rightly held that the machine hall was defective within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB during the periods in dispute and that the rent was reduced by operation of law, so that what the defendant retained within the measure of that reduction was never owed. On its order of 2 March 2023 the Senate inspected the race, its head gate and the storage part of the hall in the presence of the parties; the inspection confirmed the Landgericht's findings on the race and the gate, and the appeal raises no concrete objection to those on the gauge readings, so that all of them bind the Senate (§ 529 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 ZPO).
II.

The mill at Sanden is entered in the water register as an old right, preserved when the modern water statutes came into force; the entry, which the defendant has not disputed, records the upkeep of the race, its gates and the flood protection of the mill buildings as the burden of the holder of the right. The right to lead the creek out of its bed into the race and to use its flow for the wheels of the mill rests on that old water right. It belongs to the owner of the mill property; it runs with the mill and not with whoever happens to work in it. It gives the owner the water. It does not give the owner the water free of what the water requires.

The duty is the counterpart of the entitlement. Whoever is permitted to draw a creek out of its bed and to lead it past his own buildings must keep the works by which he does so in a condition in which the water goes where the right allows it to go and nowhere else. That comprises the race, its walls, its head and tail gates, and the flood protection of the mill buildings. The Senate has already held for the mills on this creek that water which a working gate would have kept out is not high water but the owner's omission (Senate, judgment of 27 October 2020 – 12 U 19/20).
III.

The plaintiff's submission that the water belongs to the nature of the object let, and is therefore the tenant's affair, is not followed. What the parties owe each other is determined by § 535 Abs. 1 Satz 2 BGB: the landlord must maintain the object in a condition fit for the contractual use for the whole term. A hall let for the storage and working of goods is not in that condition when the creek reaches its floor. The nature of the object may shape what a tenant may expect, but it does not transfer the landlord's duty of maintenance; nor is knowing that a mill stands on a creek knowledge of a defect under § 536b BGB (8th Civil Senate, judgment of 19 September 2017 – 8 U 52/17).
IV.

It follows that the jammed head gate was a defect from the report of August 2020 and remained one until it was freed, and that the silted race wall is a further defect of the same origin. Neither the plaintiff's budget nor its wish to settle the future of the letting first suspends the duty (8th Civil Senate of this court, judgment of 3 June 2014 – 8 U 7/14). That the plaintiff would also answer to the riparian neighbours under § 1004 BGB for water sent onto their land only confirms on whom the burden lies; it does not lighten it toward the tenant.
V.

The reduction of 40 per cent assessed by the Landgericht for the eleven months concerned lies within the estimation permitted by § 287 ZPO and is not attacked in figures. What remained unpaid after it, 3,040 euros, stayed below two months' rent and thus below the threshold of § 543 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Nr. 3 lit. b BGB. The residual default at the consecutive dates, some 190 euros a month, is no not-insignificant part of the rent within lit. a, so that neither limb is met and the termination did not end the lease. Costs follow from § 97 Abs. 1 ZPO, provisional enforceability from §§ 708 Nr. 10, 711 ZPO; there is no ground to admit the appeal on points of law (§ 543 Abs. 2 ZPO).

subject: Measuring the reduction for a storage annex flooded on nine dates: full reduction for the annex on the flood days, a standing reduction between them

titelzeile: Rent reduction for a flooded storage annex: full reduction on the ingress days, a standing reduction between them
tenor: The Senate intends to dismiss the appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 6 June 2024 - 7 O 88/23 - by unanimous order under § 522 Abs. 2 ZPO.
The plaintiff is given opportunity to state its position on this notice, and to consider withdrawing the appeal, within three weeks of service of this order.
The value in dispute for the appeal proceedings is provisionally set at 1,773 euros, that being the part of the rent claim which the chamber dismissed.

gruende.text: The appeal of the plaintiff against the judgment of the Landgericht Grevenau of 6 June 2024 - 7 O 88/23 - is admissible, but the Senate is unanimously satisfied that it has no prospect of success, that the matter has no fundamental significance, that neither the development of the law nor the securing of a uniform case law requires a decision of the appellate court by judgment, and that an oral hearing is not called for. The Senate therefore intends to dismiss the appeal by order under § 522 Abs. 2 ZPO and gives the plaintiff opportunity to state its position beforehand.

The plaintiff let to the defendant, a seed-cleaning business, the hall on parcel 61/4 of the Grevenau land registry together with the storage annex built against its northern wall, at a rent of 2,400 euros a month. The annex lies below the level of the Greven creek and is protected by a sluice gate which the plaintiff's own caretaker reported jammed in February 2022. In this action for arrears the chamber allowed the defendant a reduction of the rent and dismissed the claim in the amount of 1,773 euros. It held nine dates of water ingress into the annex to be established, each falling within two days of the gauge at the Grevenau weir exceeding 1.80 metres.

On each of those nine dates the annex stood under water for the whole working day; on the days between them it remained dry. The chamber treated the jammed sluice gate, and not the high water, as the defect. That is correct. High water in the Greven creek is a natural event, but water which a working gate would have kept out falls within the landlord's sphere (Oberlandesgericht Grevenau, judgment of 27 October 2020 - 12 U 19/20). A gate reported jammed is a defect from the report onwards, and budgeting the repair for a later year is no discharge (Senate, judgment of 3 June 2014 - 8 U 7/14).

The reduction is measured on the part of the rent attributable to the annex and not on the whole rent, because the hall itself remained fully usable throughout. The chamber estimated that part at 25 percent of the agreed rent, that is 600 euros a month or 20 euros a day, having regard to the annex's floor area, its plainer fitting-out and its subordinate function. Such an estimate belongs to § 287 ZPO and is open to review only for an error of principle; none is apparent. For each of the nine days on which the annex was wholly unusable the reduction is accordingly 100 percent of that part. Fault is not required (Senate, judgment of 24 April 2012 - 8 U 99/11).

For the intervals between those days the chamber allowed a standing reduction of 15 percent of the annex's share, and the Senate agrees. While the gate remained jammed the annex was dry but not safe: moisture-sensitive goods could not be kept there, because the creek could rise again at any time and the defendant had two days' warning at most. A room which may be entered but cannot be used for its contractual purpose of storage is impaired in its suitability within the meaning of § 536 Abs. 1 BGB, and the impairment lasts as long as its cause does. The tenant need not wait for the next ingress before reducing.

The computation follows from that. The impairment ran from the first ingress on 7 March 2022 until the gate was repaired shortly after the last, that is eighteen months at 90 euros a month, together with the difference between the full daily amount and the standing amount for the nine days, which gives the 1,773 euros the chamber allowed. The plaintiff's objection that a reduction may run only on the day of an ingress misconceives the defect, which is the gate and not the water. Its further objection that 15 percent is arbitrary is an attack on an estimate for which the plaintiff itself offered no material of its own.
